The Goff outlier dud happened last week, finishing as the QB21 against the Vikings' chaotic defense. Despite that, Goff is the QB4 in EPA per dropback and pacing for 4,770 yards with 36 passing touchdowns. He's the QB6 in fantasy despite not having anything to show with his legs.

The Week 9 environment is pristine against a Miami defense allowing 20.8 half PPR points per game to QBs (sixth). Opposing quarterbacks have moved the ball against the Dolphins regularly, including recent outings from Joe Burrow (24.6 points), Geno Smith (23.5 points) and Drake Maye (22.4 points). Miami is struggling on play action and throws over the middle. That's the entire Lions offense. Detroit is listed as 7-point road favorites with a 28.75-point implied team total (third).

9. Jayden Daniels (vs. LAR) - 17.8 proj. points

Jayden Daniels has been the QB15, QB3, QB7 and QB16 in his healthiest games. Since returning from an elbow dislocation, the Commanders have yet to call a designed run for him. He'll still scramble like a madman, but more of those are resulting in slides and running out of bounds early, too. This will hurt him on the margins, though he's still the QB1 in rushing yards per game (47.2).

The Rams present a fun matchup dynamic, ranking 21st in half PPR points allowed to opposing QBs (17.0 per game) but fourth in points allowed specifically to QB rushing. Opposing offenses facing Los Angeles also feature a 47% neutral pass rate, the third-lowest rate allowed in the NFL. Washington hosts this contest as 5.5-point home underdogs carrying a 21.0-point implied team total (23rd).

10. Trevor Lawrence (at BAL) - 18.8 proj. points

Lawrence is up to QB2 overall in EPA per dropback. He hasn't been pushed many times this year, so he's left fourth quarters without adding to his totals. He's only the QB16 in yards per game, leaving him with QB8 fantasy points per game. That's closer to his floor while everyone is healthy on offense. His ceiling is far higher when games are tighter.

That's the issue with the Thursday Night Game against third-string QB Joe Fagnano. The Ravens are 10-point dogs with a team total below 15 points. The Ravens defense is far more talented and far better coached than their current No. 15 ranking in fantasy points allowed to QBs, too. Nice field position and the occasional 1-on-1 loss downfield with Marlon Humphrey in coverage are enough to combat these minor risks for T-Law as a low-end QB1. The Jaguars are ninth in team total (24.75).

11. Tyler Shough (vs. CLE) - 16.9 proj. points

Update: Jordyn Tyson and Kelvin Banks will play. That's a big deal.

Shough is off the bye and it's possible WR Jordyn Tyson makes his debut and LT Kelvin Banks (ankle) returns after a prolonged absence. Those would be major upgrades. Shough's been the QB7 in fantasy points per game but was exposed versus the Vikings and Steelers recently while dealing with a broken non-throwing hand. He should be largely over that now, and the added rushing element has made him a low-end QB1 at times in the fastest-paced offense:

Week 9 presents a much tighter test against Cleveland, as the Browns rank 26th in half PPR points allowed to opposing QBs (15.2 per game). They haven't been tested by above-average QBs this entire month, however, with Aaron Rodgers, Cam Ward, Tyler Huntley and Geno Smith in their recent history. The Browns play man coverage more than anyone else, but the Saints have the WRs to hang in there. New Orleans is listed as a 2.5-point home favorite with a 23-point team total (14th).

12. Jordan Love (at NE) - 17.5 proj. points

Love is playing the sport like nobody else. His absurd aggressiveness and arm talent are amazing to watch every week.

Love has turned into the QB9 on a per-game basis, with the second-most yards per game (281). His top three pass catchers are healthy, and they're starting to figure out the best starting OL and ways to hide them on the margins. He's scored multiple touchdowns in 7 of 8 starts. Even with Josh Jacobs in the fold, the Packers have maintained their pass-first identity. That's how it should be behind this OL.

His Week 9 draw is tougher on paper against a New England defense that ranks 22nd in half PPR points allowed to quarterbacks (16.6). The Packers head on the road as 3-point road underdogs with an implied team total of 22.25 points (17th). That's lower than normal.

13. Malik Willis (vs. DET) - 17.0 proj. points

The Dolphins are definitely better in November than in September. This is the youngest team in the NFL, and it's a new scheme with a new QB. The team is gelling, while also getting healthier at OL and WR. Willis has been fantasy's QB7 since Week 5 on QB14 EPA per dropback. Some of that is because of a Caleb Douglas sideline YAC TD, but him being in the lineup is helpful! Miami is still 30th in neutral pass rate (44%), but they'll be forced to pass here.

The Lions have allowed the most fantasy points to QBs, and opposing offenses have the third-highest neutral pass rate allowed. Their run defense is simply better than their secondary. Detroit will miss star LB Jack Campbell over the middle (and I really hope things progress for him, beyond football), but they did get star S Brian Branch back recently. The Lions have given up the seventh-most rushing QB points this year, partially because of garbage time scrambles. Those count for us! Willis will try to continue this top-12 QB streak, after Kyler Murray (QB10), Jordan Love (QB12), Jacoby Brissett (QB7) and Bryce Young (QB7) have done just that this month. Miami carries a 21.75-point implied team total (18th) as 7-point home underdogs.

14. Matthew Stafford (at WAS) - 18.1 proj. points

Stafford doesn't look fully healthy right now. Some of his sideline and downfield attempts lack his usual zip, and his throwing motion is feeling a little more Philip Rivers-like. I wasn't surprised to see Monday's report that his elbow is sore. That's what his throwing motion looks like right now, and the offense being extremely quick-hitting is further evidence of just that. Over the past month, Stafford's average depth of target is at just 5.4 yards downfield. The good news is the Rams have remained top-five in neutral pass rate in the two games without Davante Adams. Stafford is a lower-ceiling QB2 right now. He is fantasy's QB16 this year on QB16 EPA per dropback.

He now faces a Washington defense allowing the third-most half PPR points per game to quarterbacks (22.0). Opposing passers have found plenty of success against the Commanders, who rank sixth in QB passing points allowed per game. Jameis Winston tagged them for 326 yards and three passing scores in Week 5, while Brock Purdy posted 17.4 fantasy points the following week with backups at WR. The Rams enter as 5.5-point road favorites with a 26.5-point implied team total (eighth).

16. Michael Penix (vs. CIN) - 15.5 proj. points

17. C.J. Stroud (at LAC) - 16.9 proj. points

18. Kirk Cousins (at SF) - 16.6 proj. points

19. Drew Lock (vs. ARI) - 15.1 proj. points

20. Baker Mayfield (at CHI) - 15.0 proj. points

21. Bryce Young (vs. DEN) - 14.9 proj. points

22. Daniel Jones (vs. DAL) - 14.7 proj. points

23. J.J. McCarthy (at PHI) - 15.2 proj. points

24. Carson Wentz (vs. BUF) - 14.1 proj. points

25. Geno Smith (at KC) - 13.6 proj. points

26. Justin Herbert (vs. HOU) - 13.6 proj. points

27. Shedeur Sanders (at NO) - 14.5 proj. points

28. Joe Milton III (vs. NYG) - 13.7 proj. points

29. Gardner Minshew (at SEA) - 11.3 proj. points

1. Brock Bowers (at SF) - 76.5 proj. yards

Bowers' 17.2 half PPR points per game are on flirting with the best of all time at the position. He's barely even a tight end in this Klint Kubiak offense, one that's experimenting at RB and OG because the ground game is so broken. He peaked just last week with a season-high 24.7 half PPR points on 21.0 expected points. That rarely happens. Same with his 40% target share.

I know the 49ers have LB Fred Warner roaming the middle, but the 10-point spread is going to lead to a hilarious amount of targets on the road here. This is a good matchup on game script alone.

2. George Kittle (vs. LV) - 68.5 proj. yards

Update: Mike Evans (Achilles) and Deebo Samuel Sr. (hamstring) are out. Demarcus Robinson is back. This past month with injuries at WR, Kittle has been the TE4 on TE5 usage, commanding a 29% share in each of the past two games with Evans in and out of the lineup.

San Francisco draws a Raiders defense giving up 14.8 half PPR points per game to tight ends, the fourth-most in the league. The 49ers are 9.5-point home favorites with an implied team total of 31.25 points (first). Smash spot, duh.

3. Colston Loveland (vs. TB) - 52.5 proj. yards

Since Week 6 when Caleb Williams returned, Loveland is the TE3 on TE4 usage, largely competing with George Kittle for that No. 3 spot behind the truly elites of Brock Bowers and Trey McBride. That momentum was capped by a 7-catch, 69-yard showing on 12 targets with a 40% target share in Week 7.

Tampa Bay ranks 12th in half PPR points allowed to TEs at 12.1 per game. They've been an elite run defense (31st in rush YPG), and their outside CBs have stood out on tape, too. Where they've been most vulnerable is through the air over the middle, where Loveland operates. When they plan man coverage, Loveland has a matchup advantage here. Chicago is listed as 5.5-point home favorites with an implied team total of 26.5 points (7th).

4. Trey McBride (at SEA) - 59.5 proj. yards

The Cardinals no longer have the following skill players: Marvin Harrison Jr., Kendrick Bourne, Jalen Brooks, Reggie Virgil, Jeremiyah Love and Bam Knight. McBride was already the TE1 overall in usage, but his rare volume is further insulated. Gardner Minshew is known for his garbage-time dropbacks.

Of course, it's never a fun time against the Seahawks defense. They've allowed the fewest passing yards per game (169.1) and the fourth-fewest points to TEs. Colston Loveland (65 yards), Travis Kelce (44) and George Kittle (24) all had fairly quiet outings against them this month. McBride has battled against them recently, too. He was the TE9 on TE2 usage in Week 2, while finishing as the TE1, TE15, TE7 and TE2 in his other games against Mike Macdonald. A 14.75-point team total is scary for his touchdown odds, even if he'll likely see 8+ targets again.

5. Tyler Warren (vs. DAL) - 41.5 proj. yards

My PPR Scam senses are tingling. Warren saw 8 targets upon return from a groin injury last week, and the Colts might be shipping Jonathan Taylor, Josh Downs, and/or Keenan Allen after this game. Throughout the year, Warren is the TE7 on TE6 usage. He's mixed in at the goal line and his intermediate role has come and gone depending on the matchup. A 29% target share last week is worth chasing, especially with the matchup looking way friendly this time out.

Dallas ranks 18th in half PPR points allowed to tight ends (10.9 per game), but the main point is the Colts have a solid 22.75-point team total (15th). Dallas has had issues in zone coverage, and they haven't had quality play at S and LB2. Trey McBride had his typical TE3 overall week last Sunday against them.

6. Sam LaPorta (at MIA) - 43.5 proj. yards

LaPorta sits as the TE8 on TE6 usage across his last four games, averaging 10.8 half PPR points on 10.5 expected points. His weekly involvement has swung drastically, ranging from a 13-target explosion for an 8-84-1 receiving line and a 25% target share against Carolina in Week 4 down to just two targets and a 6% share versus Green Bay in Week 7. Over this 4-game stretch, he has averaged 6.3 targets and 55.8 receiving yards per contest while maintaining an 18% target share. With all Lions, it's best to take a zoomed-out average and live with the ups and downs.

The Dolphins have been among the league's most accommodating matchups for the position, ranking third in half PPR points allowed to tight ends with 15.8 per game. Miami has already surrendered massive individual outings, including a 13-catch, 119-yard TE2 finish to T.J. Hockenson in Week 4 and a 2-touchdown TE1 day to Mason Taylor in Week 7. Detroit heads on the road as 7-point road favorites carrying an implied team total of 28.75 points (third). Miami has been lit up on play action routes to TEs, specifically. It's a get right spot.

7. Travis Kelce (vs. NYJ) - 45.5 proj. yards

Things have cooled for Kelce after leading the dang NFL in yards after the catch through the first three weeks. He's only the TE23 on TE16 usage this past month, bringing him down to TE8 on TE14 usage in 2026. That's a fair baseline for now, but the return of Rashee Rice certainly does not help his mid-range TE1 chances. He had an 18% target share last week with him back for example versus a 26% share in Week 7. The good news is his rough schedule lightens up here after facing the Seahawks and Broncos most recently.

The Jets rank 16th in half PPR points allowed to tight ends at 11.1 points per game. New York just surrendered a massive multi-touchdown performance to Brock Bowers (24.7 half PPR points, TE1) in Week 8, along with top-10 weekly finishes to Greg Dulcich (11.1 points, TE9) in Week 7 and Hunter Henry (12.8 points, TE8) in Week 6. Kansas City is listed as 9.5-point home favorites with an implied team total of 28 points (fourth). It's a great spot.

8. Isaiah Likely (at PHI) - 45.5 proj. yards

Likely did nothing (TE25 usage) in a tough matchup with the Texans in Week 7, which was JJ McCarthy's first start in New York. They had the bye week to get on the same page. McCarthy was willing to let things rip downfield in ways Jameis Winston couldn't, but Likely is too important to the offense as a de-facto slot receiver and No. 2 target for the on/off splits to hold to this degree. I'm giving Likely another chance before really reacting to the QB switch. It's helpful that Cam Skattebo (hamstring) is doubtful with Najee Harris released and Tyrone Tracey Jr. (hamstring) placed on IR. They likely can't run as much as they'd like to this week.

The Eagles have been the 3rd-best defense against the position, but Likely is more of a slot than true TE. They haven't had the best season from SCB Cooper DeJean, while S2 and LB2/3 have been major problems. Chig Okonkwo was this close to a massive game last week and Brenton Strange had 68 yards in Week 5. They haven't faced top-end TE play in a long time. The Giants are 3.5-point road favorites with an implied team total of 21.5 points (20th).

9. Tucker Kraft (at NE) - 45.5 proj. yards

Kraft ranks as the TE9 on TE9 usage over his last four games, producing 10.6 half PPR points and 9.5 expected points per game. His involvement has remained steady throughout that span, recording between 5-8 targets in each contest with an average 17% target share. He has hit the end zone in back-to-back weeks. The return of Josh Jacobs will only hurt on the margins, leaving Kraft as an upside low-end TE1.

New England ranks 23rd in half PPR points allowed to TEs, giving up 9.2 per game. On film, they are much easier to attack here versus on the perimeter with their star-level CBs. Colston Loveland was the TE3 in Week 7 and Brock Bowers was the TE2 in Week 5, proving just that. Green Bay enters Foxborough as three-point road underdogs with an implied total of 22.25 points (17th). I'm still surprised this game total is as low as it is with both QBs playing well.

10. Kyle Pitts Sr. (vs. CIN) - 41.5 proj. yards

Kyle Pitts is the TE5 on TE10 usage over his last four games, averaging 11.4 half PPR points and 9.4 expected points per contest. His lone dud was last week's rain storm shutout. He's been a low-end TE1 with Michael Penix otherwise on a 20% target share. Atlanta has leaned heavily on the run this season, posting a 44% neutral pass rate that ranks 31st (second-lowest) in the league, but being at home against an offense that will score often helps get the dropback count up.

The Bengals present an inviting setup through the air, ranking eighth in half PPR points allowed to TEs with 13.0 per game. Cincinnati has surrendered weekly finishes inside the top 10 at the position in two of its last four games, including Brenton Strange's 7-95-0 line (TE6) in Week 4 and Gunnar Helm's 5-76-0 line (TE8) in Week 8. Those aren't players who typically drop 75+ yards. It's one of the worst LB duos on tape, and their safeties have been missing tackles, too. The Falcons are 3-point home underdogs with an implied team total of 24.25 points (12th). A lot of this has to be Pitts in the underneath and intermediate.

11. Harold Fannin Jr. (at NO) - 44.5 proj. yards

The reality of the Browns is there is more skill talent than team points to go around. Fannin, like Denzel Boston, KC Concepcion and Quinshon Judkins, has been extremely up-and-down. This season, he's the TE10 on TE9 usage, seeing TE6 targets per game. Fannin didn't have a screen target for the first six weeks, but those have returned in each of the past weeks. I wouldn't be surprised if coach Todd Monken dialed up a couple of them here with Shedeur Sanders less trusted than Deshaun Watson in this offense. Sanders' floor is just as low as Watson's in a one-game sample. We're firmly in the boom-bust range now.

The Saints represent a favorable landing spot, ranking 6th in half PPR points allowed to TEs at 13.8 per game. New Orleans has given up significant production over the middle lately, including a 6-99-1 receiving line and a TE1 weekly finish to Isaiah Likely in Week 6. Cleveland travels as 2.5-point road underdogs with an implied team total of 20.5 points (24th).

12. T.J. Hockenson (vs. BUF) - 42.5 proj. yards

Hockenson is the TE11 on TE11 usage this season, as the primary check-down in the offense while Justin Jefferson frequently gets double teamed and Jordan Addison runs vertical clear out routes. Carson Wentz will look to right the ship with Kyler Murray "hurt". I wouldn't change Hockenson's projection much because of the QB change, however. He's been great against the worst TE defenses (TE2 vs. MIA and TE7 vs. DET) but has been forgettable against the good ones.

Buffalo ranks 17th in half PPR points allowed to tight ends at 11.0 points per game. They've allowed at least 62 yards in 3-of-4 recent games to the top TE, including TE7 and TE10 finishes to Michael Mayer and Tyler Higbee. This is a clean individual matchup for Hockenson.

13. Hunter Henry (vs. GB) - 35.5 proj. yards

Last week's foot injury kept him out of practice on Wednesday and Thursday, but he was limited on Friday and the Patriots didn't activate another TE on Saturday. He's on track to play. They need him with A.J. Brown and TreVeyon Henderson out. Henry has been the TE11 on TE18 usage this past month without AJB playing much.

The matchup is a difficult one. The Packers have the best safety trio in the NFL, though their LBs are pretty banged up. They've allowed just 7.0 half PPR points to the position on average this year (31st). Sam LaPorta (18 yards) and Colston Loveland (19) had slow games against them this past month. New England stays home as 3-point home favorites with an implied total of 25.25 points (10th).

14. Brenton Strange (at BAL) - 35.5 proj. yards

15. Dalton Kincaid (at MIN) - 44.5 proj. yards

Kincaid is difficult to get right. He's scored below 3.3 half PPR points three times and has finished as a top-five TE three times. Kincaid's role isn't changing all that much, but as a vertical-based TE, it's easier for his targets to fall off out of nowhere. Last week's role was pretty great, though, ultimately finishing as the TE5 in expected half PPR points after multiple 2/3-TE set explosives and an isolated first-down completion against the great S Kyle Hamilton. He had a 19% target share then with D.J. Moore back. I'm just taking the longest sample possible, which is a TE9 on TE13 usage baseline this season.

Unfortunately, the Vikings represent a stingy draw on paper, ranking 32nd in half PPR points allowed to tight ends at just 5.5 per game. Minnesota's opponents have posted a neutral pass rate of 45% (lowest rank 2 of 32 teams), which suppresses overall aerial opportunity. On top of that, TEs and RBs are often kept in to block, which isn't Kincaid's strong suit. It wouldn't be a surprise if his routes were lower than normal. Buffalo enters as 3.5-point road favorites with an implied team total of 25.0 points (11th).

16. Mike Gesicki (at ATL) - 26.5 proj. yards

Gesicki is running pure. This season, he's the TE6 (!!!) on TE21 expected half PPR points per game. To his credit, he's done it week after week, finishing as a top-20 TE in all but one game (HOU in Week 2). Gesicki is only the TE33 in targets per game (3.3), but his red zone chemistry with Joe Burrow has made that concern mute so far. Gesicki did have a season-high 66 air yards last week for what it's worth.

Cincinnati travels as 3-point road favorites with an implied total of 27.25 points (6th). The Falcons rank 10th in half PPR points allowed to TEs, surrendering 12.5 points per game to the position. Most recently, George Kittle (88 yards) and Colston Loveland (TE4) have had their usual good games against them.

17. Dallas Goedert (vs. NYG) - 39.5 proj. yards

I can't say Goedert is moving around well. That was a tough adjustment and drop that led to the interception over the middle in Week 8. He hasn't cleared 9.1 half PPR points since Week 1, and I wonder if his days on the Eagles are coming to an end given his expiring contract and the return of Eli Stowers. He's the TE18 on TE14 this month, despite not having DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks for most of it. A trade would be the only way Goedert gets back into the fantasy TE1 mix, and most of the contending teams have a nice starter.

The Giants rank 22nd in half PPR points allowed to tight ends, giving up 9.4 points per game to the position. 19. Dalton Schultz (at LAC) - 34.5 proj. yards

#2884. Trump targets Slotkin in call for DOJ probe of alleged Democratic threats to Republicans

President Donald Trump said Saturday that he was ordering the Justice Department to investigate Democratic leaders over what he described as threats against Republican officials, donors and supporters, without identifying the alleged communications or providing evidence of criminal conduct.

"The Democrats are going around threatening a lot of people, including the Attorney General of the United States, and others, with Impeachment and many other forms of punishment, even though they admit they have no reason to do so," Trump said in a Truth Social post.

The alleged threats, the president said, are "extortion at the highest level," he wrote. "I am ordering the Department of Justice to look into this criminal act, immediately!"

In his post, Trump claimed that Democratic Sen. Elissa Slotkin of Michigan is planning to "go after all young people that believe in Republican Values."

Trump was apparently referencing a speech Slotkin made at a University of Chicago event on Oct. 13. At the time, Slotkin said: "I want young people coming out of school to say, 'Should I go work for the Trump administration?'...I want them to be like, 'Lord, that might be buying myself a ton of problems that I don't want. And so let me avoid participating in that.' I want that deterrence message sent."

Slotkin alleges that she, her family and her staff faced physical and legal intimidation after the posting of a November 2025 video in which Slotkin and other Democratic leaders called on the U.S. military to "refuse illegal orders" following the airstrikes targeting boats in the Caribbean.

On Nov. 20, Trump called the video treason and said "an example must be set."

The FBI contacted lawmakers, including Slotkin, days later. In February, Slotkin declined to sit for an interview the Justice Department requested about the video.

"The intimidation is the point, and I'm not gonna go along with that," the senator said in February. A federal grand jury later declined to indict the video participants.

Now, Trump alleges Democrats are threatening legal intimidation against Republican leaders and their supporters.

"Republicans should get smart, fast! Threatening letters have been sent to many people, all innocent, from Democrat Political Leaders," the president wrote.

The White House and Slotkin didn't immediately respond to a request for comment.

#2883. Risk of Iran war escalation remains high despite Democratic sweep in U.S. midterm elections

The U.S. and Iran are careening toward renewed war despite growing hopes this week that the Democrats' decisive midterm election victory will bring the conflict to an end, analysts say.

Crude oil prices fell more than 16% over the last five trading days after U.S. Vice President JD Vance publicly blamed the Republicans' stinging loss on the war. Vance's remarks raised questions about whether the administration still has support to continue the conflict with Iran.

The Democrats plan to use their comfortable majorities in both chambers of Congress to pass a war powers resolution that demands President Donald Trump end the war. But tensions in the Middle East have not eased since the election, and the Democrats aren't sworn in until January, the analysts say.

"Throughout the week, we were struck by the divergence between deepening escalation concerns in the Gulf and the headline-driven off-ramp optimism of market participants thousands of miles away," Helima Croft, head of global commodity strategy at RBC Capital Markets, told investors in a note Friday.

Late Saturday, U.S. Central Command said it disabled a St. Kitts-flagged ship after the tanker ignored multiple warnings and attempted to leave the region after visiting an Iranian port, according to media reports. Iran state media also reported on explosions on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, as well as several blasts occurring in the port of Jask. CNBC couldn't independently confirm the reports.

Several oil tankers have also come under attack near Oman since the election, killing one seafarer, according to maritime security agencies. Iran's Houthi allies in Yemen continue to fire missiles at neighboring Saudi Arabia.

Meanwhile, the U.S. military buildup continues, with a third carrier strike group en route to the region. The consulting group Rapidan Energy sees an 80% chance that fighting will resume as diplomacy stalls.

Trump told reporters Thursday that he will make a decision soon on whether to attack Iran again.

"I would rather not destroy the rest of the country if possible but maybe I'll have to," Trump said in the Oval Office. "You'll know soon enough."

"We're locked and loaded," the president said. "If we have to do the rest of the Iran thing, we're very much locked in."

Crude oil prices will vault above $100 a barrel again in response to renewed fighting, said Bob McNally, president of Rapidan and a former energy advisor to President George W. Bush. Brent crude, the international benchmark, traded above $97 on Friday, while U.S. crude was around $90.

"President Donald Trump is determined as a legacy item, almost at all costs, to prevent Iran from getting a nuclear weapon, having them give up their nuclear capabilities," McNally told CNBC's "Squawk Box Asia" on Friday.

"The Iranian regime, on the other hand, is not willing to do it," the analyst said. The escalation dynamic remains in place so long as that core difference between the U.S. and Iran persists, he said.

The risk of war is still alive, especially since Trump no longer faces future elections, said Amos Hochstein, a former energy advisor to President Joe Biden. Gasoline, diesel and jet fuel prices would all surge as a consequence, Hochstein told CNBC's "Power Lunch" Friday.

Tehran has been taunting the Trump administration since the election. The social media account of Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei said the "process of the U.S.'s collapse has accelerated" after the midterm results.

And Congress is unlikely to pass a war powers resolution until Democrats take control in January. Trump can veto such a resolution anyway.

The main leverage Congress will have is the power of the purse, Croft said. Government funding expires on Dec. 11, and negotiations for another continuing resolution could drag into 2027, she said. This would give Democrats more leverage when they take power in January, the analyst said.

"Importantly, deferring funding decisions would not immediately constrain Trump's ability to conduct military operations, but could significantly reshape the administration's longer-term funding outlook," Croft told investors.

Trump discussed diplomatic efforts to de-escalate tensions in the region with the emir of Qatar during a Friday phone call, according to Qatar's state news agency.

An unnamed senior Iranian official told Reuters on Thursday that Tehran sent a nuclear proposal to the U.S. through Qatar. Tehran will only discuss the proposal after the U.S. meets its demands, the Iranian official told Reuters.

Trump seemed to dismiss the diplomatic efforts Thursday.

"Iran will never have a nuclear weapon," the president said. "They're not doing anything without our approval. It doesn't make any difference what they're looking at," he said of the diplomatic efforts.

#2882. Hardik Pandya-Arshdeep Singh trade: What do MI and PBKS stand to gain from the deal

Hardik Pandya-Arshdeep Singh trade: What do MI and PBKS stand to gain from the deal originally appeared on Cricket News. Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

Hardik Pandya is set to join Punjab Kings in exchange for Arshdeep Singh, with the trade reportedly completed.

Mumbai Indians, who finished ninth in IPL 2026 with four wins from 14 matches, gain a left-arm new-ball and death-overs specialist to pair with Jasprit Bumrah.

Punjab Kings gain a fast-bowling all-rounder under Shreyas Iyer but take on Hardik's injury risk and lose their all-time leading wicket-taker.

After months of trade rumours and uncertainties, Hardik Pandya's home ahead of the 2027 IPL might be decided in the most shocking way possible. According to multiple reports, the Mumbai Indians and the Punjab Kings have agreed on one of the biggest trades in IPL history, with Hardik Pandya moving to Punjab and Arshdeep Singh going the other way ahead of IPL 2027.

An IPL source has confirmed that the trade has been completed and that Hardik is pleased to play under Shreyas Iyer, who continues as Punjab's captain. Hardik's three-year stint as Mumbai captain has been disappointing, with the franchise making the playoffs just once and losing 24 of their 39 matches.

In contrast, Arshdeep has been in excellent form in recent seasons, even helping Punjab reach the finals against RCB last year. His 111 wickets in 96 matches at an economy rate of 9.18 has also been a big part of his appeal.

Both teams have until the retention deadline on November 17, and the mini-auction takes place in Goa on December 16. Here is what each side stands to gain.

MORE: 'GG never accepted mediocrity' - Iyer reveals Gambhir's high standards with KKR

The clearest gain is bowling support for Bumrah. No Mumbai bowler took more than 15 wickets in IPL 2026, with Allah Ghazanfar leading the list with 15. Arshdeep took 14 wickets for Punjab in the same season and 21 in 2025, when he led their attack to a place in the final.

He also brings a skill set that complements Bumrah. In April, he took 3/22 against Mumbai by swinging the new ball, reversing the old one and bowling a quiet over in the middle. His record at the death is built on yorkers, and a Bumrah-Arshdeep pairing gives Mumbai two specialists for the last four overs.

The deal also resets the captaincy. Rohit Sharma is expected to regain the role, which ends a tenure that produced more defeats than wins.

MORE: Livingstone reacts after R Ashwin's co-host compares him to 'trash'

Punjab finished fifth in 2026 with seven wins from 14 matches and were among the last teams to be eliminated, so the gap to the top four was small. A fast-bowling all-rounder is the rarest profile in T20 cricket, and Hardik was the first player in that category to score 1,000 runs and take 100 wickets in T20Is.

The fit is also clean off the field. Hardik joins purely as a player, with Iyer staying in charge, and the decision to trade for him came from the captain and the coach.

The risks are real, however. Hardik has suffered multiple injury breakdowns and has not played since the last IPL, and Punjab are giving up the bowler who is the franchise's all-time leading wicket-taker.

MORE: Arshdeep Singh-Hardik Pandya swap: Fans react as R Ashwin drops major hint over MI-PBKS trade deal

On paper, Mumbai has addressed a specific issue by bringing in a proven specialist. They needed a second front-line pace option beside Bumrah, and Arshdeep is a better fit for that role than any bowler on their 2026 wicket list. A fresh captain and a fit new-ball partner give a ninth-place side a clear route back into the top four.

Punjab's logic is harder to read. Their second-half bowling was a major issue last season, and they have traded away their best bowler to fix it. That only works if Hardik stays fit and bowls meaningful overs, because an all-rounder who misses games cannot make up for the loss of a leading wicket-taker.

A side that reached the 2025 final deserves the benefit of the doubt, but the deal puts all of the risk on Hardik's body.

The trade will be judged on two numbers: how many league games Hardik plays for Punjab and how well Arshdeep and Bumrah share the death overs for Mumbai. Punjab's answer to replacing Arshdeep's overs will be revealed at the Goa auction on December 16.

#2881. Lakers vs. Pistons Preview: Strength vs. strength

The Lakers (8-2) embark on their first true road trip of the season on Sunday, starting with a stop in Detroit to take on the Pistons (6-2). This is the first contest of a four consecutive games away from home.

Who: Los Angeles Lakers at Detroit Pistons

After a home-heavy start to the season, the Lakers will hit the road for their first road trip of the season, starting with the stiffest test of the slate.

The red-hot start from the Lakers and Luka Dončić offensively has them ranked as the top offense in the league. The Pistons, meanwhile, enter the contest with the best defense in the league, pitting strength vs. strength.

Like Portland, Detroit plays a physical defensive style to try to overwhelm opponents. Offensively, that hasn't deterred the Lakers in either matchup against the Blazers, but Detroit is arguably the best in the league at that style of play, so it'll be a tough test for the purple and gold.

Like the Lakers, the Pistons excel at steals and blocks on the defensive end. However, they are simply average at rebounding, unlike the Lakers, which allows them to close out possessions and bolster their defensive rating.

Detroit allows the third-fewest wide-open 3-point attempts and teams have hit the fewest wide open threes against them in the league. That stat will be put to the test against Luka and Austin Reaves, depending on how they opt to scheme against them defensively.

One area the Lakers could find success is getting to the line. The Pistons put opponents on the line often, ranking 24th in the league in opponent free throw attempts. The Lakers are fourth in the league in free throw attempts per game.

After battling one of the Western Conference's top teams on Friday, the Lakers will have another tough test on Sunday afternoon against one of the East's elites.

It'll be an interesting test for the purple and gold, and another chance to see how they respond to top competition.

Detroit has been off since losing to the Sixers on Wednesday, so this will be a well-rested Pistons team.

After playing in Friday's G League opener for the Coachella Valley Lakers, both Cameron Carr and Bronny James are joining the parent team on the road trip

Luka is a new addition to the injury report with back tightness as he's listed as questionable. It's the same injury that led to him missing a game against the Clippers earlier this season.

Jalen Duran (hamstring strain) remains out for the Pistons while Isiah Joe is also out with a right hip contusion.

#2880. The Good, The Bad, and The Ugly: Notre Dame Fighting Irish 2026 Edition

The playoff fight now begins. Miami traveled to South Bend to face off against Notre Dame, and lost 31-24. This is Miami's first loss of the season, and now makes the path to the playoffs a bit more arduous.

Craig T. Smith has your recap from the bitter loss.

And now, let's get into The Good, The Bad, and The Ugly

QB Darian Mensah. Gotta put him somewhere, guys, and this doesn't mean I think he was perfect. Far from it. Still, I'd classify his performance more here than other places (though, there are moments that I excoriate later in this piece). 24/43 passing (55.8% completions) for 276 yards with 3 touchdowns and 1 interception, and 11 carries for 28 yards rushing.

Mensah's cumulative stats: 211/276 passing, 76.4% completions, 2,701 yards, 28 touchdowns, 2 interception, 35 carries, 137 yards, 2 touchdowns.

WR Cooper Barkate. Reminded y'all how good he is. 10 catches for 92 yards and 2 touchdowns

TE Elija Lofton. 7 catches for 113 yards and a touchdown.

RB Mark Fletcher Jr. 13 carries for 57 yards and 1 catch for 4 yards.

LB Mo Toure. 12 tackles including a couple of HUGE run stops on 3rd downs.

LB Chase Smith. 8 tackles and a QB hurry.

LB Kamal Bonner. 6 tackles and some really nice plays in his first extended action since he transferred here last year.

P Dylan Joyce. 43.8 yard average on 5 kicks.

K Jake Weinberg. 1/1 on FGs and 100% touchbacks on kickoffs again.

Holding Notre Dame to a field goal on their first drive. Nice stops on 2nd and 3rd down ended the momentum.

This stop by S J.J. Dunnigan was instrumental to getting that stop for a FG.

A great punt by Dylan Joyce, and the best punt coverage tackle this year by LB Cam "Bobby" Pruitt.

Nice blitz by Chase Smith on 3rd down to end Notre Dame's 2nd drive.

K Jake Weinberg hit a 19yd FG to get Miami on the board.

Good stop by the defense on the drive after Miami's FG to force a punt after 5 plays.

Mensah to Lofton 12 yard touchdown to finally find the endzone midway through the 3rd.

REALLY GOOD tackle in space on a swing screen by LB Kamal Bonner.

Miami forced the first 3 and out of the game with this PBU by CB Damari Brown on the next play!

Touchdown Hurricanes! Darian Mensah to Cooper Barkate for a 12 yard touchdown and we have a ballgame!

And Miami forces another 3 and out on the ensuing drive! This run stop by Toure on 3rd down was massive and got us the ball back!

Another Mensah to Barkate touchdown brings Miami back within a touchdown

Mensah to Lofton on a broken/extended play gains 41 to put Miami in prime scoring position, down a touchdown late in the 4th quarter

10 chunk plays — 7 passes (15+), 3 runs (10+)

Going away from the run game early. I thought we were rolling, but didn't stick with it.

Allowing a 4th down conversion at midfield on the first defensive drive of the game.

Pass rush not being able to get home vs. Carr. This is something they've struggled with all season.

Getting pushed around up front and a DT batting down a 3rd down pass late in the 2nd quarter.

Mensah missed a few throws today. Yes, he was pressured, but also just missed some. Had a touchdown to Jacobs up the sideline early in the 4th quarter and it was very late and woefully underthrown.

An even time of possession. 29:05 for Miami, 30:55 for Notre Dame

This was much the same as last week vs. Carolina, and 4 minutes under Miami's average for the year

Advanced Stats show a close game, but one where Miami came up short. It tracks.

Seriously, the only teams worse to lose to than these pompous assholes are Ohio State and Florida, in that order. Can't STAND those bastards.

Another week allowing an opposing QB to do numbers against the defense.

Another week with little to no pressure from the pass rush, linemen only or blitz package. Regardless of the scheme, it didn't get home.

Season-low 377 yards of offense (1 yard less than the Wake Forest game, which was a blowout and then all that weird stuff happened)

TECHNICALLY the final play was a fumble by Barkate on the lateral attempt recovered by Notre Dame, for those wondering about the accounting here

That turnover and the ensuing touchdown were the difference in this game. That hurts.

Not blocking ND's star DE on the first 3rd down of the game. Fletcher had no shot on the play, and was immediately tackled for loss. Miami's drive stalled and the Canes punted.

Illegal block in the back on ND uncalled on the last play of the 1st quarter. Allowed them to gain 26 yards, because the block sprung the play. No call. Cool.

DB Bryce Fitzgerald getting beat for a touchdown. Took a perfect throw, but still. Miami went down 10-0 with the play.

On the ensuing kickoff, holding, Cam Pruitt.

On this same drive, 6 plays inside the 5 and settling for a FG. That's not good enough.

Offsides with contact, Justin Scott. Gifted Notre Dame a 1st down on 3rd and 2.

Armondo Blount jumped offside at the hard count on the same play. Spared the flag because Scott's penalty was worse.

Offsides, Marquise Lightfoot. Declined with a completion for 22.

Holding, SJ Alofaituli. 1st play of the 2nd half.

Allowed a 56 yard punt return to open the 2nd half. ND started on the Miami 30.

QB Darian Mensah threw his 2nd interception of the year on an out route toward Lofton. Miami was making a comeback push after consecutive touchdowns on offense and 3-and-outs on defense. Notre Dame extended the lead to 31-17 on the ensuing drive after this pick.

This fan's reaction to the interception above was all of us in the moment, and an instant meme. This is Michigan surrender cobra level stuff. An all-timer and we all knew it the moment we saw it.

Miami having a miscommunication with coverage on 4th down, allowing the RB wheel route to be wide open to covert and gain 33 yards.

DB Damari Brown not staying down after the play when hurt. He got up and tried to stay in the game, but then went down. Because he did that after the ball was spotted, Miami was assessed a timeout. In the 4th quarter of a game with these stakes and circumstances, that timeout could be crucial.

Facemask, Justin Scott. Give Notre Dame 1st and goal instead of 4th and goal. Irish scored a touchdown on the next play.

Miscommunication on a huge 3rd down. Multiple guys go with the crosser, nobody went with the RB on a wheel route. Backbreaker.

Notre Dame committed a clear DPI on Daylyn Upshaw on 3rd and goal. They held his arms as he went up to attempt a leaping catch. No call. REALLY terrible, but that's what happens when you leave it up to the refs.

The next play, the would-be tying and potentially go-ahead touchdown catch by Elija Lofton ruled incomplete. It's the right call because the rules say you have to complete the catch through contact. It's just ugly because we needed this so so so badly.

Mensah getting sacked/taking a sack on the 1st play of the last drive. Need a touchdown, no timeouts. You CANNOT take a sack there my guy.

Notre Dame CLEARLY targeting Mensah on the 3rd down play 2 plays after the previous bullet point. Crown of the helmet to Mensah's helmet by the defender. No call. THEN not called after review. Absolute bullshit.

Let me be clear here: Miami lost. There were bad calls that happened. Those calls did not cost Miami this game.

The first half gameplan was very "17 year old true freshman QB starting his first game" vibes to me. VERY tight and conservative in moments where some air, space, levity, SOMETHING was needed. The offensive line was terrible tonight. Mensah did his best to overcome the constant pressure, but it took until after halftime to get any rhythm going. Settling for 3 points after 5 plays inside the 5 was a killer. And yes, the absence of Malachi Toney is massive, but Miami is better than they showed offensively for the majority of this game. I liked the rhythm in the 2nd half, but the interception was an absolute killer, and the points Notre Dame scored from it were the margin of victory. And yes, I know this is the best team we'll play this regular season. But I still needed more from the offense.

Pass defense still has issues, but Miami finally started to look competent on that side of the ball again. They forced multiple 3 and outs, and played with a physicality that had been lacking recently. There were still penalties and missed tackles and communication issues, and plenty of points allowed, but there were signs that this defense can do enough for Miami to win. Not today obviously, but moving forward. I just hate that it had to get to 24-3 for them to show up.

Punting was good, but punt coverage allowed a 56 yard return. Kicker made his FG, and was perfect on PATs and kickoffs. There was another penalty on specials giving Miami terrible field position. One step forward, two steps back for this unit.

Another game where it seemed like Miami was not ready to meet the moment. Notre Dame was fully keyed up heading into this game, the stadium was raucous and fans at a fever pitch…..and Miami was just there. Shannon Dawson didn't have a good gameplan without Malachi Toney, and it took until the 2nd half to really start cooking. Corey Hetherman's performance was much the same. And Mario Cristobal went BALLSITIC on the refs at the end over the Lofton no TD play, but that's a badge of honor in my eyes. Still, it took Miami going down 24-3 for them to get things going in the right direction. The team looked as though they were neither ready nor prepared for this game. Missing 1 player, even someone as good as Malachi Toney, cannot have that result.

Got punched in the face. Time to get back up off the mat and work. But that doesn't mean I can't be critical about things…and I am.

That's it for this installment of The Good, The Bad, and The Ugly.

#2879. Meta chief strategy officer Dave Wehner leaves to join AI infrastructure startup Fireworks as CFO

Dave Wehner, Meta's chief strategy officer, is leaving the company for four-year-old AI startup Fireworks.

At Fireworks — an AI inference and model-training platform focused on open models that was valued at $17.5 billion during a Series D fundraising round in July — Wehner will assume the CFO role, he announced on X on Friday.

Wehner will be tasked with scaling the company's finances and operations, Fireworks CEO Lin Qiao said in a statement to CNBC.

"Fireworks has the right mission for the moment," Wehner wrote on X, adding: "I've become increasingly bullish on what they are building. There's a remarkable depth of technical talent here, coupled with a very practical focus on what customers need."

The AI startup, founded in 2022 by former Meta and Google employees, is a platform that lets developers customize and run open models for their businesses. Its latest investment round was led by Atreides Management, Index Ventures and TCV, but Fireworks is also backed by Nvidia and Sequoia Capital. Business Insider reported that it is in early talks to raise funds again at a possible $30 billion to $40 billion valuation.

Wehner joined Meta, then called Facebook, in 2012 and was the company's chief financial officer from 2014 to 2022.

"Dave helped guide Meta through tremendous growth and complexity over 14 years, and brought disciplined thinking to some of our hardest company-level decisions," Meta COO Javier Olivan said in a statement to CNBC.

Fireworks is notably smaller than Meta — the tech giant has about a $1.56 trillion market capitalization as of Friday's close — and its competitors, which include OpenAI and Anthropic.

"Dave told me he wanted to get back to a smaller company where he could build toward a big impact again," Fireworks' Lin wrote in a LinkedIn post on Friday. "He sees AI as the defining technology shift of his lifetime and wants to help shape what comes next."

The company's size has not made it immune to the risks and complications often associated with AI technology. In October, the company found "a security incident involving unauthorized use of internal Fireworks credentials," in which "an unauthorized third party accessed environment variables used in evaluation jobs in a limited number of customer accounts," it said in a press release.

"Based on our investigation at this time, we have not detected evidence of unauthorized access to customer models, datasets, training data, personal information, or inference traffic within the Fireworks security perimeter or control," the release said.

#2878. CNBC's experts on whether the AI trade is ending and what investors should do next

Amid a powerful rout in tech stocks, investors told CNBC on Thursday that something may be fundamentally breaking in the AI trade following the big success of Democrats in Tuesday's midterm elections and the threat they try to slow the data center buildout.

Democrats are more aggressively anti-data center than Republicans, and Wall Street is quickly redoing its math what any restrictions they implement could mean for the related companies' future growth.

"Right now, investors are questioning that $1.2 trillion of capex that we forecast for next year," Peter Boockvar, chief investment officer at One Point BFG Wealth Partners, told CNBC. "Well, maybe that's not going to happen."

Boockvar believes this could be the start of the end of the AI trade as we know it.

Whether it's completely over or not, investors need to be reassessing how they're planning to play the AI trade going forward, the analysts said.

The Nasdaq Composite dropped 5% on Thursday and fell into correction territory, off by more than 11% from its record high set last month. The iShares Semiconductor ETF dropped 11% on Thursday, its biggest decline since during the Covid breakout in March 2020. The Global X Artificial Intelligence & Technology ETF (AIQ) is down 6% on the day and down 15% over the past month.

"There has been a huge change in the outlook for AI infrastructure buildout," Eric Johnston, head of equities at Cantor Fitzgerald, told CNBC. "The entire economy and the consumer and earnings growth are all levered to that buildout."

The selling Thursday spilled over to non-AI stocks with the Dow Jones Industrial average down more than 1,600 points.

Josh Brown pointed to the 4.8% yield for the 10-year Treasury yield, saying a compelling risk-free rate is causing investors to reconsider taking the risk in these volatile AI stocks.

"You don't need to be at 80% U.S. stocks and have 60% of that exposure be tech," Brown said.

Many investors believe the AI trade isn't over completely, investors just need to get more selective.

"The AI buildout just got harder," said Rob Sechan, Newedge Capital Group Founder & Managing Partner:

"Nobody voted to make compute less scarce," Sechan said, citing Microsoft's Azure cloud business growing 48% year over year in its most recent third quarter. That level of growth suggests its capacity constrained, not demand constrained, he said.

"When new capacity gets harder to build, existing capacity becomes more valuable," Sechan said.

Richard Clode, portfolio manager at Janus Henderson, noted a few bright spots in tech on Thursday despite the highly correlated downward movements in the big tech indices.

"Motorola Solutions had some good results," he said. "We're seeing a little bit of rotation into some of the … internet names...Sony reported some good results, and again they were up strongly overnight."

"So there are some brief pockets of respite from this, but obviously pretty painful across the board today," he said.

Some experts believe the selling was overdone and investors could start nibbling.

This "indiscriminate selling" is a "buying opportunity," said Larry Adam, Raymond James chief investment officer. If investors "take a longer term perspective, which is what we do, I think the valuations at today's levels will tend to prove to be a good buying opportunity," he said, urging investors to look at the fundamentals.

Victoria Greene, chief investment officer of G Squared Private Wealth, said she saw some strong supports around the S&P 500's 200-day moving average and was on the lookout for a market bounce following Thursday's rout.

"Typically, the average return is plus about 180 basis points the next day," she said. "The question we have to ask ourselves: Is this a pullback in an uptrend, which is what I believe? Or is this the end-all, be-all [and] the wheels are coming off and everybody just needs to buy T-bills? I don't think we're there yet."

#2877. 31-year-old dumpster diver brought in $140,000 in 12 months: I 'did much more than I thought was possible'

When Carter Stevens tells people he makes six figures a year digging through dumpsters, they often assume he's "blowing smoke," he says.

Not everyone sees dollar signs in a brimming dumpster. But Stevens earned roughly $140,000 in total sales between September 2025 and September 2026 by salvaging trashed items, cleaning them up and selling them on platforms like eBay and Facebook Marketplace, according to documents reviewed by CNBC Make It.

Stevens primarily operates near office parks and luxury condominiums around Nashville, Tennessee. Since March 2024, when he started dumpster diving, he's found and sold hand-crafted Persian rugs, high-end office chairs and even samurai swords, he says. Trash-picking helps him keep his shipping costs low, he adds: Some of his supplies, like cardboard boxes and packing tape, also come from dumpsters, enough that he doesn't have to pay for them approximately "90% of the time."

"The amount of waste in this country that you'll find is unbelievable. We throw so much stuff out," says Stevens, 31.

Sometimes, Stevens asks a building for permission to go through its trash, marketing himself as a junk removal service. In that way, his job is similar — though not identical, because he generally only takes what he can sell, he says — to other entrepreneurs across the U.S. who follow advice in Reddit threads or YouTube tutorials to launch junk removal side hustles or full-time businesses. There are around 10,000 junk removal businesses across the U.S., according to the Better Business Bureau. They range in scale from independent side hustles to national companies like 1-800-GOT-JUNK, which touts more than 150 franchise locations.

Other times, Stevens finds himself neck deep in rubbish, ducking concerned security guards, peeling away actual trash and rotting food in the hope of uncovering discarded treasure, he says. He tries to avoid sneaking around and keeps an eye out for "no trespassing" signs. He'd rather leave items behind if a property owner or security guard tells him to vacate the premises, he says.

Even Stevens expresses surprise at how much money he's made, saying he doesn't necessarily think his annual income is sustainable. When he "stumbled into" dumpster diving, he was approximately $12,000 in debt after years of poor spending habits fueled partially by a drug addiction, a stark change from his affluent childhood, he says.

"I dug myself out of a hole. I built up my savings. I really did much more than I thought was possible," says Stevens.

Stevens, a Nashville native, is the son of a five-time Grammy Award-winning producer of country and gospel music who has worked with artists like Blake Shelton and Carrie Underwood. His life took a turn in college when he developed an addiction to prescription Adderall, leading him to drop out partway through his senior year in 2018, he says.

His lack of a college degree made landing full-time work a challenge. He says his parents can afford to support him financially, and they've done so in specific emergency occasions. But mostly, his father wants his kids to learn to fend for themselves, he says: "He will let me sit on the coals for the sake of learning how to swim. That's taught me a lot [and] given me a lot of valuable skills and a tough mentality."

Unemployed, Stevens started combing through thrift shops and Goodwill clothing racks for vintage apparel to sell on eBay. He was inspired by YouTube influencers like Rick Senko, he says, whose Fort Lauderdale, Florida-based clothing resale business Technsports brought in $6.5 million in annual revenue as recently as 2024.

But Stevens' returns were inconsistent, and he often spent his profits on drugs or luxury shopping sprees, he says. After his parents funded a rehab stint in 2021 — helping him "quit doing the hard drugs," he says — he spent his money chasing other dopamine hits. Those indulgences included a $1,200 pair of Christian Dior Birkenstock sandals, an 85-inch flat-screen television and a $30,000 down payment on a Mercedes-AMG sedan that he later lost because he couldn't afford the total cost, he says.

By June 2023, he could no longer afford to pay rent, so he lived in a rented storage unit until the business's security found and evicted him, and then stayed in his Nissan Sentra for three weeks, he says. Homelessness shocked him into learning to manage his "reckless" spending habits, he says: "Being punished by your own spending addiction was a wringer that I promised myself I can't be put through again."

In October 2023, a cousin lent him money to start renting an apartment, and Stevens worked to stick to a sensible enough budget for his thrifting income to cover future rent and basic expenses, he says. Five months later, he found a discarded pair of black Nike Air Force Ones in good condition next to a gas station pump. He took them home, sanitized them and sold them online for $35, he says.

"That was the first time I had ever found something that was trash and sold it and made a little bit of money," says Stevens.

Once he started dumpster diving, Stevens was hooked "because I never stopped finding good stuff in these dumpsters," he says.

His biggest score to date: dozens of discarded Steelcase office chairs, worth $1,000-plus each when new, outside an overflowing office park dumpster, he says. He got his car — by this point, a used pickup truck and a self-built trailer — and hauled away 190 chairs to list online at hundreds of dollars apiece. He sold the majority of them in bulk transactions on Facebook Marketplace for $17,000, and brought in an additional $10,600 selling the remaining chairs individually, documents show.

If Stevens manages to find roughly one valuable haul per month, he can fill his $400-a-month storage unit and start listing the items. For the most part, he scopes out corporate environments, preferring "dry dumpsters" over ones laden with food waste, he says. Office trash is particularly profitable when companies downsize, says Stevens: Once, he found 120 standing desks discarded outside a building.

Near high-end apartment buildings, Stevens has found furniture from brands like West Elm, iPads, electronics and power tools in working condition, he says. "Almost every piece of furniture in my apartment came from a dumpster," says Stevens.

Stevens works alone and minimizes gas costs by sticking to locations within a few miles from his apartment. The majority of his income has come from big hauls across his five highest-earning months, reflecting the venture's hit-or-miss nature. "I got really lucky earlier this year and I made a ton of money. I'm not acting like this is something I could do every year," he says.

So he saves as much of his earnings as possible, "constantly" talking himself out of unnecessary purchases, he says. And he's studying the business of real estate wholesaling — which involves securing contracts for distressed properties and flipping them to investors for a fee — as a potentially more secure way to earn a living, he adds.

Still, he acknowledges the allure of knowing his next big payday could always be one dumpster away.

"I don't see myself ever turning down a good looking dumpster," says Stevens. "I have found so much cool stuff that I feel like I'll always be curious about what's in that dumpster."

#2876. Mark Cuban says he doesn’t ‘give a f---' about growing his net worth—a healthy mindset for non-billionaires too, a financial therapist says

Mark Cuban has zero F's to give — at least, when it comes to his net worth. Financial therapists say that's a healthy mindset to have, even if you're not a multibillionaire like Cuban.

"I don't give a f--- about my net worth. I have enough. My family has enough," Cuban posted Monday on social media platform X, responding to another user's post about the growth of the serial entrepreneur's wealth going back to 1990.

"I don't care about moving up on the Forbes 400," Cuban added.

Cuban currently has an estimated net worth of $6.8 billion, according to Forbes, which ranks the former star of ABC's "Shark Tank" as the 597th wealthiest person in the world. Cuban sold his first business, a software company called MicroSolutions, for $6 million in 1990. He became a billionaire when he and his co-founders sold Broadcast.com to Yahoo for $5.7 billion in 1999.

He developed his attitude after buying a majority stake in the NBA's Dallas Mavericks in January 2000, he tells CNBC Make It: "I was more interested in winning than making money." The mindset might seem obvious to some: After all, why would a billionaire have any stress about his bank account? But even people with lots of money experience financial stress and anxiety, studies have shown.

What seems to set Cuban apart from some other wealthy people is the confidence he exhibits in how he puts his wealth to use, says Christine Hargrove, an Athens, Georgia-based financial therapist. In his post, Cuban wrote that he doesn't obsess over growing his personal net worth because, in part, he'd rather see the impact his money can have on the world.

"My next dollar can impact other people's lives a lot more than mine," wrote Cuban, citing his decision to launch the cost-cutting pharmacy startup Cost Plus Drugs and his many small-business investments across 15 seasons on "Shark Tank" as an investor judge. "That is what drives my investments. I look for ways to have an impact."

Confidence in how you save or spend your money is often a signal of a healthy financial mindset, notes Hargrove, who is president-elect of the Financial Therapy Association and Assistant Director of the Love and Money Center at the University of Georgia.

"You actually have to be the person to decide what is enough for you," she says, adding: "Having a sense of purpose with your money and with your life can be an incredible source of protection against chronic financial anxiety."

Many Americans, especially as costs of living remain high nationwide, have no choice but to worry about their finances.

When those with plenty of money in their bank accounts or stock portfolios obsess over their level of wealth, they're also probably not doing so by choice, notes Hargrove. Some people's financial insecurities come from growing up in low-income households. Others may think of themselves as relatively struggling because they earn less than the other wealthy people around them.

"Having a healthy relationship with money isn't just about how much you have. It's about understanding what money means to you and what you want it to do for you," says Cara Macksoud, an Orlando-based accredited financial counselor and financial behavior specialist.

No matter what your financial situation is, anxiety about money can actually hurt your finances in addition to the toll it takes on your mental health. Financial stress and related mental health challenges can hurt workplace performance through distraction and absenteeism, according to a 2024 report by the TIAA Institute, the research arm of retirement fund manager TIAA. Poor mental health can also impair cognition, making it more difficult to make sound money decisions, the report suggested.

Obsessing over every dollar can also make it feel impossible to part with money for causes that would otherwise align with your personal values, such as charitable giving or support for loved ones, Hargrove says. "And then our money actually comes between us and who we want to be," she adds.

Financial anxiety often results in repetitive behaviors, such as obsessively checking your bank account or stock portfolio, notes Hargrove. For those not in immediate financial peril, Hargrove suggests reminding yourself "enough is enough" and working to replace those behaviors with actions that foster gratitude for the cherished aspects of your life that are not related to your finances.

If you constantly check banking apps on your phone, you might change your wallpaper to a photo of your family or friend group to remind you of the safety of your family and social networks, for instance. It's a simple trick, but it can soon become part of a pattern of "focusing on thoughts of gratitude" that research has shown can lower levels of the stress hormone cortisol in your body, Hargrove says.

And if you can feel like you're using your money to make a positive difference, whether for yourself or others — as Cuban suggested in his post that he does — you probably have a healthier mindset around money than a lot of other Americans, notes Hargrove.

"Living with gratitude and feeling like you make a difference, either for yourself or for other people, [there's] not much better than that in life, right?" Hargrove says.

#2875. ‘We Squashed It’: Hamilton Denies Demands as Leclerc Calls Ferrari Saga Closed

Lewis Hamilton says there were no demands from either side in his talks with Charles Leclerc, as both Ferrari drivers try to move on from their Mexico clash.

The Ferrari saga should now come to an end after the latest comments from Hamilton and Leclerc, following their meeting on Thursday. Team boss Frederic Vasseur reminded both that the F1 team should always come first at all costs.

There are still no set rules of engagement, as he feels it is self-explanatory that the two teammates have to be careful if they are on track together. In the meantime, Italian media reported demands from Hamilton's side.

The reports said Hamilton wanted preference for the rest of the 2026 F1 season since he is ahead of Leclerc in the championship. But the Brit denied any such demand, saying he and Leclerc had talked it through.

"Me and Charles sat and spoke, and we squashed it, and we're moving on," Hamilton told Sky Sports F1. "We still have a huge amount of respect for each other, and I'm glad we had a chat, and now we move on.

"We've been getting along just fine as normal. Sometimes, in those scenarios, it takes having a conversation, and there's been no demands from either side; it's both just giving our points and areas we can do better and support each other. I'm hoping to have better races moving forward."

Lewis Hamilton in qualifying at Interlagos. Image Credit: Scuderia Ferrari

Ferrari teammate Leclerc, meanwhile, took some time away for the birth of his daughter. He arrived in Brazil late and went straight into the meeting. For him, it is a closed chapter after good discussions with Hamilton and even Vasseur.

"I mean, from my perspective, I was very straightforward, of course, and I think it was good to speak," Leclerc told the media. "I think this is always needed after a moment like this. It took proportions that are way too big, and it has been around also for way too long.

"At the same time, it was a very special week for me, so I couldn't really have those discussions before. And it was important to have those discussions, but now I consider that a closed chapter, and I think it will be important to look ahead."

A Ferrari in the wet at Interlagos. Image Credit: Scuderia Ferrari

Leclerc feels it is okay to disagree, but better to speak your mind, as they did. "I really believe that when we speak, things are much better straight away," he said.

"Of course, there is tension; of course, we want to finish ahead of each other, and sometimes we are not going to do things right. And it's okay sometimes to disagree on the way you see things, but at the same time, discussing about those things helps a whole lot.

"I mean, history speaks for itself, and maybe, yeah, looking back, it's maybe something needed. At the same time as I said, sometimes you disagree, and you've got to find common ground."

Asked about Hamilton saying that Leclerc races harder against him than anyone else, the Monegasque didn't want to add fuel. "I wouldn't want to comment on that," he said. "Honestly, there have been way too many comments, and again way too much fuss about it for way too long, so I don't really want to get into those kinds of comments."

#2874. Things you should know about the newest Raptor, Kevin McCullar Jr.

Kevin McCullar Jr. is the newest addition to this Raptors' roster, joining Toronto on a two-way deal earlier this week on November 5th. The former New York Knick is a 25 year old small forward, standing at 6'6" with a 6'9" wingspan.

After being waived from New York to make space to sign Dalton Knecht, McCullar Jr. joined the Raptors. The leader of the Big 12 in scoring in his senior year, he was an All-American on the Kansas Jayhawks before turning pro. In the NBA, his biggest role came in his sophomore year with the Knicks, where he played in 21 games, including a stretch of matchups when Josh Hart went down with an injury.

From our sister site Posting and Toasting, an idea begins to emerge about who he is beyond the stats. Writer Michael Zeno said that the forward exhibited "pure hustle" while being a threat from deep off the catch-and-shoot, with a penchant for picking up some unnecessary fouls.

TORONTO, CANADA – OCTOBER 13: Kevin McCullar Jr. #9 of the New York Knicks handles the ball during the game against the Toronto Raptors on October 13, 2026 at the Scotiabank Arena in Toronto, Ontario, Canada. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this Photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Mark Blinch/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images

From his highlights, you see a shooter with good form, someone who can knock it down past the arc while remaining competent closer to the basket. Having spent time in the G League, the Westchester Knicks made a video interviewing him about his personality, on and off the court. He called his stepback his "go-to move", which he said was his main way of independent shot creation.

This offensive toolkit is certainly something that the Raptors require. Being able to play without the ball in your hands, to allow for the Raptors' arsenal of creators to set the flow of the offence, while not freezing up when executive decisions need to be made, sounds like just what the doctor ordered for this Raptors team. Jamison Battle is the teammate comparison that comes immediately to mind; and while the forward has not yet developed the same reputation as a knock-down shooter, his development further him along in that direction.

In the G League, McCullar Jr. averaged nearly 17 points and six assists, along with three stocks per game, showing some two-way capabilities. He'll likely spend a lot of time on the Raptors 905 developing further, and bolstering a team which just lost its first matchup to the College Park Skyhawks this week.

McCullar Jr. could be the next Raptors success story, developing well and making it out of the G-League to become a productive pro. In a situation where it feels like a roster shakeup is inevitable, the Raptors are taking this first step to bolster the team's shooting.
