#2843. Marcus Freeman made his point without saying a word. Notre Dame believes

SOUTH BEND, IN – Four minutes after kickoff, and less than two minutes into Saturday night's latest iteration of the decades-long Miami-Notre Dame feud, Fighting Irish coach Marcus Freeman said everything he needed to say to his team.

Instead, Notre Dame's rock-star popular leader — think Elvis, Taylor Swift, hell, on this night, think the program's most adulated head man since the late Lou Holtz, whom Notre Dame honored — basically nodded his head.

CFP rankings live predictions: We have a new No. 1, and it's bye bye, Buckeyes

His Irish offense faced 4th-and-1 at midfield. Sophomore tailback Nolan James Jr., generously listed at 5-10 and 215 pounds, battered through the Miami front for four yards.

Seven snaps later, Notre Dame kicked a field goal. It led 3-0 and never trailed the rest of the game, a 31-24 Irish win.

"If you're nervous on a fourth-down call versus Navy, you're going to be nervous versus Miami, right?," Freeman told USA TODAY Sports. "Like the decisions I make when we go for it on fourth down have nothing to do with the opponent. It had to do with what we believe, what I believe in terms of when we go for it on fourth down.

"So, I didn't want the game to influence decisions. We have a plan. We've just got to go out there and execute, and our guys executed when it mattered the most."

What Freeman clearly believes about this team must now be confronted by the rest of college football: The Irish, with one of the highest-paid rosters in the sport this season, are three more wins from a return to the College Football Playoff.

Their stellar sophomore quarterback, CJ Carr, delivered the signature performance of his 21 career starts. He threw for 319 yards and three scores on 29-for-40 passing. He ran just once, for three yards, but it set up what proved to be the decisive touchdown plunge from James.

Carr was never sacked. The Irish never turned over the football.

Notre Dame converted another fourth down in the fourth quarter. James validated that decision four snaps later.

"Just the confidence that coach Free has in us as an offensive unit," said wideout Micah Gilbert, whose nine catches, 98 yards and two scores were all team bests. "It's great to see that we have four downs at times to get that first. Honestly, just him trusting us with that."

Miami, Notre Dame's first No. 1-ranked victim since Clemson in 2020, turned over the ball twice.

Quarterback Darian Mensah, who entered as the Canes' last remaining Heisman Trophy contender following Malachi Toney's midweek ankle injury, was sacked twice, hurried four times and knocked down by Notre Dame's finally unleashed pass rush.

Battered but never broken, Mensah still threw for 276 yards and three scores. His only real blemish was an interception by Irish safety Luke Talich, when the former Wyoming walk-on jumped a route directly in front of his jubilant sideline.

Notre Dame cashed in the miscue for a game-steadying touchdown.

The Hurricanes, however, mustered just three touchdowns in five red-zone trips.

Twice in the first half, they were handed goal-to-go first downs because of Notre Dame defensive penalties. Six consecutive snaps from at or inside the Irish 10 culminated with Notre Dame edge Boubacar Traore terrorizing Mensah in the gap.

See, that moment did the same thing as Freeman's fourth-down gusto: It sent a message.

"Unbelievable," Carr said of that sequence from his defense. "We could feel the rise of our momentum in the first half, and that was a big hump.

"To see those guys go three-for-three after the penalty (in stops from the 1-yard line) was unbelievable and definitely fueled us in the next couple drives."

Meanwhile, Miami coach Mario Cristobal fueled the sport-wide, season-long angst over officiating with a mini-rant to open his postgame comments.

Facing 4th-and-6 from Notre Dame's 18 with less than four minutes left, Mensah fired toward the left corner of the south end zone, opposite Touchdown Jesus and Notre Dame's famed golden-domed Main Building.

Already a touchdown scorer, Elija Lofton elevated for Mensah's toss and dragged a foot through the end zone and onto the white paint. But Talich never relented on the play and dislodged the ball.

Even upon review, the ACC crew upheld the on-field call.

An incensed Cristobal excoriated the crew.

"Really disappointed that they negated Elija Lofton's touchdown with two hands on the ball and two feet in bounds," Cristobal told reporters. "But like we told our team before we left Miami, do not leave it in the hands of officials because that's what you're going to get here. …

"Very disappointed with the way that was called with the game on the line and clear possession of the football in bounds."

Of course, that's the same officiating crew that twice whistled those aforementioned penalties, giving the Canes goal-to-go first downs they failed to turn into touchdowns.

The same crew flagged the Irish seven times for 57 yards, compared with five penalties for 31 yards against Miami.

Unlike too many contests this season, this game wasn't won or lost on officiating mistakes or mysterious game-clock mismanagement.

The Irish won with belief and, ultimately, better execution.

"I know it's a big one; this is big," said Freeman, now with 18 wins against ranked foes — including dispatches of teams ranked No. 1, 2, 5 (twice), 9 and 20 since 2022. "This is special. I'm not going to sit here and this is like the other ones. No, this is different. There was a lot of emotion, a lot of physical preparation, but mental preparation we put into this.

I want them to enjoy it, but tomorrow it doesn't do anything for the future."

That might be the only time Freeman said something that didn't involve believing.

Because the Irish won this game, they still have a future.

And it looks an awful lot like a return engagement with the CFP.

#2836. “What Are We Doing Here?”: Blazers Announcers Call Out Victor Wembanyama for Abusing NBA Loophole

Victor Wembanyama once said he was glad to be part of "beautiful, pure and ethical basketball." Yet the San Antonio Spurs star has continued to face accusations of flopping from rival fans and broadcasters. That debate resurfaced against the Portland Trail Blazers, whose announcers went from expressing concern for Wemby to openly questioning the calls going his way.

The criticism was aimed at the frequency of the French star's trips to the floor and the officials' decisions to award him free throws. With 30 seconds left in the second quarter and San Antonio leading 62-47, Dylan Harper missed a three-pointer, but Victor Wembanyama secured the offensive rebound. He then went to the floor after what appeared to be minimal contact from Deni Avdija, whom the officials called for a loose-ball foul.

The call did not sit well with the Moda Center crowd. As the replay appeared on the Jumbotron, fans immediately booed the decision. Avdija reacted by placing his hands on his head, while that was enough for the Portland announcers to lose patience. "That guy spends more time on the floor than anybody I've ever seen. You've got to be kidding me."

"Yeah, that's not alright. What are we doing here? That's not alright," the announcer said.

The frustration from the Blazers fans and the broadcasting team arose because Victor Wembanyama scored all of his eight points in the second quarter from the charity stripe. The reaction from the announcers first began with some concerns.

Wemby appeared to consider a three-pointer, but Sidy Cissoko closed out on him. The Spurs center went down during the sequence, prompting the Portland broadcast crew to react.

"So it's good to see him pop back up. I don't want to see anybody out there hurt. Blazers want to play the best of the best," they added,

There was no immediate accusation of foul-baiting. The commentator simply wanted to see Wembanyama get back on his feet.

The next clip was when the Spurs were ahead 50-33, and Toumani Camara lined up a corner three. He missed, and Wemby grabbed the rebound, and then the Portland star went to contest. But Wembanyama absorbed the contact and fell. The officials called Camara for a loose ball foul. The broadcast crew questioned the contact and the foul decision involving the Portland forward.

One commentator strongly disagreed with the call.

"No, absolutely not. That is not a foul," they said.

That's why the frustration escalated as Wembanyama ended with another free-throw attempt. It also revived an ongoing discussion about whether the Spurs star benefits from a whistle that opposing teams do not always receive.

This is not the first time a rival has questioned his tendency to draw contact. In March 2026, the Spurs star drew several fouls against Jalen Duren and Ron Holland, and his frustration spilled onto social media.

"C'mon, bruh, this is crazy," he said. Isaiah Stewart, the Detroit Pistons center, even tagged the official NBA refs X account, which is meant to encourage transparency with fans and educate them about the rules.

The controversy is about the perceived inconsistency in how officials judge contact. Portland's announcers believed the calls involving Victor Wembanyama deserved closer scrutiny, especially after multiple disputed sequences.

Now, Wemby's 7-foot-4 size also makes some of these plays difficult to judge. With his presence, the Spurs ultimately pulled away, scoring 45 points in the third quarter before completing a 125-103 win. Victor Wembanyama finished with 29 points in just 24 minutes, shooting 9-of-13 from the field and 3-of-6 from beyond the arc.

Another criticism came after the historic night against the Dallas Mavericks. Victor Wembanyama even became the first player with a stat line of at least 52 points, 24 rebounds, and 8 blocks in league history. But it involved the San Antonio Spurs star attempting 23 free throws, three fewer than the Mavs team total. Rival head coach Dusty May criticized the refs without getting fined: "That's a lot, that's a lot. So, no, I'm new to this."

And with previous players raising similar concerns, the debate surrounding Victor Wembanyama's whistle is unlikely to disappear anytime soon.

Okongwu made a return after a short stint in the locker room and found Aaron Wiggins for this easy layup.

Flemings use his speed to get this layup.

NFL+ Premium, while a little pricier at $14.99 per month (or $80 annually), also includes access to NFL RedZone, plus full and condensed replays of every game across supported devices. NFL+ also offers a free seven-day trial.

The rumors have finally turned out to be true. After weeks of uncertainty surrounding the event, further fueled by geopolitical tensions in the Middle East, the UFC has officially confirmed its return to Saudi Arabia. The promotion made the announcement during the broadcast of UFC Vegas 124, putting an end to speculation about the event.

UFC Saudi Arabia is scheduled for December 5 at the ANB Arena in Riyadh, with Israel Adesanya set to headline against rising middleweight contender Shara Magomedov. For Adesanya, this could be one of the most important fights of his career.

ALSO READ: Islam Makhachev Accepts Colby Covington's Challenge for $200K Charity Padel or Wrestling Match

The former two-time middleweight champion is going through the toughest stretch of his UFC run, having suffered four consecutive defeats. His most recent setback came against Joe Pyfer at UFC Seattle, leaving him with plenty to prove as he looks to remain relevant in the 185-pound division.

The matchup also marks a new chapter for Adesanya outside the Octagon. It will be his first UFC appearance since parting ways with his longtime gym, City Kickboxing, in July earlier this year.

Magomedov, on the other hand, has been chasing this matchup for quite some time. The Russian called out Adesanya after defeating Michel Pereira at UFC Baku in June. That victory improved his UFC record to six wins and marked his second consecutive victory inside the Octagon.

The co-main event also promises plenty of action, with Ian Garry set to take on Yaroslav Amosov in a five-round welterweight contest. Amosov enters the matchup with an impressive 30-1 professional record, although this will be only his third appearance in the UFC.

The 33-year-old has made an excellent start to his Octagon career, picking up wins over Neil Magny and Joel Alvarez since joining the promotion in 2025. Before making the move to the UFC, the Ukrainian established himself as one of the best welterweights outside the promotion.

He went 8-1 in Bellator, captured its welterweight championship, and also became widely recognized for his service to Ukraine during the country's war with Russia. Meanwhile, Garry will be looking to get back on track following his unsuccessful welterweight title challenge against Islam Makhachev at UFC 330 in Philadelphia.

The Irishman gave the Dagestani champion a run for his money, but Makhachev ultimately secured a unanimous decision victory, extending his UFC winning streak to 17 fights. At just 28 years old, Garry still has plenty of time to work his way back into title contention.

However, beating someone with Amosov's credentials would be a significant statement. The Ukrainian is widely viewed as a potential future title contender, making this a particularly important matchup for both men.

#2825. Cavs lose to Knicks 109-97 as Brunson and Towns combine for 60 points

The Cleveland Cavaliers lost to the New York Knicks 109-97. Donovan Mitchell finished with a season-high 37 points.

The Cavs started strong for the second night in a row, showing active hands defensively in the first quarter to force three Knicks turnovers. They also held the Knicks to just 3-of-11 three-point shooting in the opening quarter.

Karl-Anthony Towns kept New York attached. He scored 14 points in the first quarter while throwing down a pair of thunderous dunks. This was a much more difficult matchup for Mobley than the previous night, when he held Joel Embiid to 0-of-9 shooting.

A Knicks run led by Jalen Brunson put New York back in front going into halftime. Brunson hit tough shots en route to 16 points in a five-minute stretch. He finished the first half with 20 points.

Cleveland trailed 63-53 at halftime. Then the Knicks blew it open in the third quarter to extend an 18-point lead into the final frame.

New York's quick-hitting offense, which thrives on off-ball movement and screening, had the Cavs perpetually lost throughout the night. James Harden struggled to navigate screens, while the rest of the Cavaliers (even Evan Mobley) weren't able to communicate cleanly enough to avoid giving up opportunities at the rim.

This proved to be a bad combination for the Cavs in last year's playoffs, and it looks like their personnel still isn't able to keep up with New York's offense.

Towns and Brunson ended with a combined 60 points. The Cavs ended this game needing far more from Evan Mobley and James Harden. The two combined for just 19 points. It felt like Mitchell was the only Cavalier who could find his shot for most of the night.

Of course, the Cavs were without some key players tonight. Jarrett Allen missed his third straight game, while Jaylon Tyson has been sidelined since before Halloween. Sam Merrill, who injured his elbow in Friday's game, was also out tonight.

Still, there's a larger trend of the Knicks simply outplaying the Cavs. Sometimes a team has your number, and it feels like the Knicks have held an advantage over Cleveland since 2023.

#2820. Parker out to cure 'desperate' West Ham

New West Ham United head coach Scott Parker has been given a crash course in the perils of leading the troubled club in his first three days in the job.

Appointed on Wednesday to replace the sacked Nuno Espirito Santo, Parker has had two away games but just one training session to work with his new group of players.

Little more than 72 hours in the post, but enough time to witness at first hand a soft underbelly on the pitch and a hostile atmosphere in the stands.

Wednesday night was the ultimate game of two halves, as they went three goals down to Cardiff City only to recover in the second half to share a point in a six-goal thriller.

But there was no comeback from a two-goal margin as they slipped to a 2-1 loss at Blackburn Rovers, a result that knocked them out of the play-off places.

And the players were left to face the ire of 7,000 Hammers fans who had trekked up to Ewood Park to see it.

Parker has become a modern-day Championship expert in recent seasons, securing promotion with Fulham (2020), Bournemouth (2022) and then Burnley in 2025, but the Hammers arguably represent his greatest challenge.

A former captain of the club in his playing days, the 46-year-old knows he must quickly ease the disconnect in place between players and fans.

The pressure is on West Ham to deliver an immediate return to the top flight and Parker's early take is that the players are feeling the pressure of that expectation.

"I see a desperate team. 100%, I see a bit of a desperate team," he told BBC Sport. "Desperate as in the sense there is a burden here at this moment.

"Like with anything when there is an expectation, whether it's an expectation of my 12-year-old son doing his maths work, that can easily become a burden.

"What I need to do is support this group and give them the belief and the confidence to show their real quality and for sure I will do that."

West Ham fans had booed their team off in midweek at half-time in the Welsh capital and they made their feelings known again at the final whistle in Lancashire.

Chants of 'You're not fit to wear the shirt' could be heard, while goalkeeper Mads Hermansen came in for particular anger from the visiting fans.

It was a difficult situation and having played for the Hammers, Parker recognises what the club's supporters want, and need to see.

"I need to turn it around and there is a lot of pain that's come over a number of years really," he added.

"I can see the pain in these players. I see a committed group. It's my job and my responsibility to try to get us pushing in the right direction.

"I connect with every single fan. I'm from where they're from. I know what they expect. I totally understand it and it's my job to fix that."

#2818. Bengals trade targets show Jonathan Taylor is a luxury the team can't afford

The Cincinnati Bengals have been down this road before.

An explosive offense held back by a below-average defense is enough to keep the Bengals from realizing their dreams this season. That was something the franchise tried to address during the offseason, making an aggressive trade for Dexter Lawrence II ahead of the 2026 NFL Draft and signing Boye Mafe in free agency.

While Cincinnati raced out to a 5-2 start through eight weeks, it has become clear Bengals will likely need more if they plan to hoist the Lombardi Trophy at SoFi Stadium in February.

NFL TRADE DEADLINE: Candidates include Derrick Henry and another Jets surprise

And allowing 36 points to the Tennessee Titans, a team typically allergic to scoring, might be exactly what the Bengals needed. It was a sign that standing pat at the upcoming NFL trade deadline isn't an option and that offseason aggression needs to carry over.

A trip to Madrid for the team's Week 9 contest against the Atlanta Falcons represents the last measuring stick game before the Nov. 11 deadline.

Here's a look at some trade candidates it makes sense for the Bengals to explore acquiring this season.

The obvious choice. Taylor has been the subject of trade rumors for most of the season, but it's clear the Colts aren't just going to let the running back leave in exchange for a firm handshake and a package of late-round draft picks a team managed to scrounge up.

Players of Taylor's caliber aren't always available at the trade deadline, but it's important to note that he is a luxury – not a necessity. Would the Bengals like to improve their running game? Probably. Does it make sense to part with a Christian McCaffrey-type package to do it? Probably not.

Given the team's other and more pressing needs, Taylor is a player that sounds good in theory. However, this isn't a video game and the Bengals aren't a team that can afford to part with a big package of draft picks in exchange for a running back – regardless of how good Taylor is.

If the Bengals insist on adding a running back, look no further than Hall. New York has given no indication it plans to trade the 25-year-old, but recent developments suggest the team should at least consider the idea. Hall has missed the last five games with a quad injury and appears set to return in Week 9. However, Hall's absence allowed Braelon Allen to emerge in the Jets' backfield. Allen has rushed for at least 100 yards in three of those five games and over the course of a full season would be on pace for 1,713 rushing yards.

It has become clear that Allen benefits from a steady workload and finds a better rhythm as RB1. Hall's return could relegate Allen to a complimentary role, something that could hurt the Jets' backfield. If the Bengals want some running back help without breaking the bank, Hall makes plenty of sense.

Reports indicated that New York wanted a third-round pick at the deadline last season. If the Bengals are serious about getting some running back help, Hall makes more sense than Taylor if the Jets make him available.

Baun blossomed into a Pro Bowl linebacker that also earned a first-team All-Pro selection after arriving in Philadelphia. He might be the perfect target to transform the Bengals defense. The soon-to-be 30-year-old linebacker has just one more season remaining on his contract and his career timeline doesn't appear to be lining up with the Eagles' competitive window anymore. Philadelphia faces a lot of uncertainty heading into the offseason and could be staring at the possibility of a rebuild.

In other words, Baun's career could be winding down by the time the Eagles are contenders again. That harsh reality opens the door for a trade to a linebacker-needy team like the Bengals, who have some youth in the room right now.

Baun is not only someone that would stabilize the second level of the Cincinnati defense, but he could also be the veteran voice that helps develop the existing group of linebackers on the team. Baun was a key piece to the Eagles' Super Bowl-winning team. If the Bengals can find a deal with the Eagles, don't be surprised if he has the same impact in Cincinnati.

There is a "help wanted" sign hanging on the door of the Bengals' cornerback room. Injuries have taken a toll on the group and Woolen is a player that should depart Philadelphia ahead of the deadline. A Super Bowl champion last season with the Seattle Seahawks, Woolen is playing on a one-year deal with the Eagles. He is a pure rental, meaning it's hard to imagine the cost to acquire him would be hefty.

With his combination of size and speed, the Bengals can solidify an outside cornerback spot by swinging a deal for the 27-year-old.

Wright broke out in 2025 with the Chicago Bears, collecting five interceptions en route to earning his first Pro Bowl selection. The cornerback only managed to ink a one-year deal with the Jets in free agency and has played in just three games this season. He is said to be "definitely frustrated" by his role, according to ESPN's Rich Cimini. And while Wright hasn't formally requested a trade, the writing is on the wall.

Cincinnati could probably acquire Wright for a late-round pick, potentially making him more realistic than Woolen – a player that could have a larger market.

Beyond the defensive line, the Bengals should look to explore every avenue for improvement on defense. In this case, that includes Baker. Similar to Baun, Baker would provide a veteran presence to the defense and continue to signal that the team is all-in on trying to win a Super Bowl this season. At age-30, the safety isn't necessarily the player he once was.

However, the eight-time Pro Bowler and two-time first-team All-Pro already set a career-high in sacks with 3.5 through eight games this season. Baker's game is primarily in the box, which wouldn't be a bad thing for a Cincinnati team also seeking linebacker help. In a way, a deal for Baker could accomplish a pair of needs with one move and allow the Bengals to seek out other candidates on the trade market.

#2810. Nets let another one slip away, fall to Hawks in heartbreaking fashion

For nearly 47 minutes, the Brooklyn Nets controlled the game against the Atlanta Hawks Saturday night in Georgia. After building a 17-point lead in the first quarter — it wasn't always pretty — but the Nets didn't trail until the final two minutes.

However, they couldn't put it away when it mattered most and fell to Atlanta, 124-121. There were some positives, most notably Nolan Traore's fast start and the late-game heroics from Mikel Brown Jr. as well as Day'Ron Sharpe's first triple-double. All of that kept them in the game but ultimately, none of it changes the result, and Brooklyn is now 2-7, still struggling to close out matchups down the stretch.

Brooklyn couldn't have asked for a much better start. They came out firing, putting up 37 first-quarter points to take a 37-27 lead. The Nets shot 73.7% from the field (14-of-19), including 6-of-10 from three, led by the fast-rising French point guard…

The ball movement was also on full display early, dishing out 11 assists on 14 made baskets. Eight different players found the scoring column, with the Nets building a lead as large as 17 before Atlanta started to chip away at the end of the frame.

Of course, it wasn't going to be that easy for the rest of the game. By the end of the first, you could already feel Atlanta gaining some ground after an ugly first few minutes. In the second quarter, they trimmed their deficit to just four, at 70-66 entering the break. Turnovers became a big issue for the Nets, allowing the Hawks to stay in the game.

The Nets committed 11 turnovers in the first half, which gave the Hawks 15 points. As Jordi Fernandez noted post-game, it was a game long issue.

"We were not consistent enough to do the right things," said the head coach And it's not about making shots. It's about, you know, trying to do the right things. Obviously, the points off turnovers, like I said before, this is a team that you know will pressure you. And we had 22 turnovers for 28 points. And that's not acceptable. That's where you lose the game."

Brooklyn also got dominated in the paint, allowing a whopping 42 points on the inside compared to their 22. Atlanta put up 39 paint points in the second quarter alone.

Despite the turnovers, the Nets still scored at a high level. Michael Porter Jr. had 18 in the first half, while Nolan Traoré continued his excellent start to the season with 15 points on 6-of-7 shooting. Day'Ron Sharpe also thrived as a facilitator, logging eight assists in the first half. He had set a career high with eight assists on Wednesday, and that number rose to 13 on Saturday, when he also came away with his first triple-double, logging 12 points and 10 rebounds. All positive, but…

The crazy part is that the Nets shot 65.7% from the field and 50% from three in the first half, yet still had just a four-point lead. When you turn the. ball over that many times, that's what happens.

The Nets started to settle things down coming out of the locker room, though. They won the third quarter, 25-22, to take a 95-88 lead heading into the final frame. While the same level of offensive efficiency wasn't there, Brooklyn's defense became more consistent and prevented the Hawks from carrying their momentum into the second half.

The turnover issues remained prevalent for the Nets, as the total reached 16 through three quarters. However, they limited the damage on the defensive end. Fernández clearly made adjustments coming out of halftime, and those adjustments played a key role in Brooklyn retaining their lead.

Despite struggling offensively through the first three quarters and missing his first seven shots, Mikel Brown Jr. came up clutch in the fourth quarter with three huge shots from deep. After entering the final quarter with just five points, he finished with 18.

However, Fernandez decided against playing his two 20-year-olds together. While Brown Jr. was leading the charge, Traore sat on the bench for the entire fourth quarter. Was it defense or does the head coach have a problem playing the two together? Fernandez admitted he went with the hot hand — Brown Jr. — rather than play his two 20-year-olds together.

"I thought that Mikel had those five straight points, and I just let him roll. Because you cannot just keep taking them in and out." he argued. "So I thought that that was the right thing to do. Was it right? I don't know."

No matter what the young Nets couldn't finish.

While the game was back-and-forth throughout, the Nets didn't give up their first lead until there was 1:26 left in the fourth quarter. The game hadn't even been tied; Brooklyn led the entire time until then. After that, though, the Nets failed to score another point and fell 124-121. The Hawks, led by Jalen Johnson, closed the game with a 14-7 run.

Fernandez said that with such a young team, it's a work in progress.

"I'm happy with what I'm seeing and the commitment and playing hard, and now the communication is way better," he said. "It seems more like a connected group. We're rebounding better, especially defensively. So, all those things are important. And it's a testament to the work that the guys put in, the coaches, and getting one percent better every day."

Saturday was a disappointing loss for the Nets. Going from up 17 and not down once to losing in the final two minutes is rough, and yet another example that Brooklyn's young core is still developing and learning how to win games. The turnovers also continued to hurt them, as they committed six more in the final frame.

The encouraging element, of course, is Brown Jr.'s strong play, especially down the stretch. It's the second time he's really risen to the occasion in big moments, with last week's loss to the Boston Celtics as another example before his rookie blunder cost them in overtime.

Final Score: Atlanta Hawks, 124, Brooklyn Nets, 121.

It was a big night for Day'Ron Sharpe. The 6'10" 25-year-old recorded his first career triple-double and the first triple-double ever by a Nets center. Sharpe finished with 12 points, 1o rebounds and 13 assists, the final figure also a record for Nets 5. It was also the Nets first triple-double in nearly a year. Nic Claxton who Sharpe replaced in the starting line up this season had a game of 14 points, 1o rebounds and 10 assists last December.

The Nets will have a quick turnaround, heading to Dallas on Sunday to face the Mavericks in the second leg of their back-to-back. Dallas enters the matchup at 5-4, coming off a 112-100 victory over the Utah Jazz on Friday.

After letting a golden opportunity slip away against Atlanta, the Nets will look to get back in the win column on Sunday. The question becomes: can Brooklyn put together a complete 48-minute performance to secure the victory? That's what they've struggled to do most consistently this season.

#2809. Northern Illinois holds off Dayton for first win of the season

Northern Illinois is winless no more. On Saturday night, in the final game of a three-game road trip, the Huskies stormed into UD Arena and left with an 81-76 win over Dayton in overtime. A 1-2 mark in Matt Majkrzak's first three games as head coach wasn't unexpected, but the win over the Flyers certainly was.

In each of its first two games, Northern Illinois played from behind. Within three minutes at Tulsa on Thursday, the Huskies were down double digits. On Monday against Grambling State, Majkrzak's squad never led, despite having a chance to win at the buzzer.

Saturday was a different story. Led by Max Weisbrod and David Douglas Jr., who have been the catalysts all week, Northern Illinois was the one with the early lead. With 11:11 to play in the first half, Weisbrod found Douglas for a 3-pointer, pushing the lead to double digits at 20-10. The triple also put Douglas at 11 points in the first 10 minutes of the game. He finished with a game-high 27 points.

Several minutes later, at the 3:57 mark in the first half, Weisbrod picked up another assist, this time to Nino Carter-Smith, who hit a 3-pointer and gave the Huskies' their largest lead of the night at 35-18. Dayton would, however, respond with a run of its own. The Flyers cut the lead to single digits on an Aiden Derkack layup in the closing minute of the first half. Derkack had a team-high 20 points for Dayton.

Two free throws from Weisbord pushed the lead back to double digits, giving Northern Illinois a 40-29 lead at the break. Weisbrod finished with 19 points, six rebounds and eight assists, helping Northern Illinois log its third consecutive game with double-digit makes from downtown.

For the first time this season, the Huskies spent the second half defending a lead, but it didn't get off to the start Majkrzak hoped. As the Northern Illinois offense went cold, Dayton cut the lead to one, opening the half on a 10-0 run with Dercack and Amaël L'Etang scoring six of the 10 points.

Finally, Douglas broke the second-half ice with a layup, giving the Huskies their first points of the frame nearly eight minutes in. Just two minutes later, a pair of free throws from Derkack gave the Flyers their first lead of the night at 46-45. Almost immediately, Douglas scored once again, regaining the lead for Northern Illinois. The lead grew to seven, but following a bucket from Landen Joseph with 5:26 to play, Dayton held the lead until the final seconds.

Down three, with the game on the line, Weisbrod became the hero for the Huskies. The fifth-year guard drew a switch, stepped back and drilled a game-tying 3-pointer with 13 seconds to play, forcing overtime.

In the bonus period, Northern Michigan transfer Bennett Basich was the shot in the arm the Huskies needed to finish the upset. Off of the bench, Basich scored seven of his nine points in overtime and converted on a pair of free throws to grow the Northern Illinois lead to 81-76 with less than five seconds remaining.

After the Huskies tipped off the season at 3 a.m. and lost a game they were favored to win, a winless week seemed like the most likely outcome. Instead they'll return to DeKalb with a big-time win and sure of one thing: Matt Majkrzak has arrived.

#2807. 2. Bundesliga: Dresden off the bottom with convincing victory over Fürth

First half goals from Robert Wagner and Ben Bobzien had the hosts firmly in control at the half. Vincent Vermeij added a second-half strike to make it 3-0 before Hendry Blank saw red for the visitors capping off a miserable evening for Fürth. Dresden made a lively start at the Rudolf-Harbig-Stadion, although Greuther Fürth initially looked dangerous going forward. The visitors came close to opening the scoring through Omar Sillah, whose effort drifted narrowly wide after a defensive mix-up, before Sacha Bansé tested Lennart Grill with a powerful effort from distance. Dynamo also threatened at the other end, with Patrice Čović missing a promising opportunity from inside the penalty area.

However, it was the hosts who eventually broke the deadlock in the 31st minute. Niklas Hauptmann did well to turn away from two opponents before laying the ball into the path of Robert Wagner, whose first-time effort took a deflection off Hendry Blank and wrong-footed goalkeeper Florian Hellstern.

Dynamo doubled their advantage ten minutes later, with Ben Bobzien finding the net in similarly fortunate circumstances. After receiving the ball from Tobias Raschl, the forward cut inside before seeing his effort deflected by Blank and loop into the top corner, leaving Hellstern with little chance of making a save.

Fürth almost reduced the deficit before the interval, with Sillah narrowly missing a cross from Gian-Luca Itter before the latter saw two efforts blocked and deflected wide. Despite those opportunities, Thomas Stamm's side headed into the break with a deserved two-goal advantage.

The hosts continued to apply pressure after the restart and effectively put the contest beyond doubt in the 55th minute. Bobzien turned provider this time, setting up Vincent Vermeij, who had the simple task of rolling the ball into an unguarded net to make it 3-0.

Fürth's evening then went from bad to worse seven minutes later when Blank received his marching orders. Having already been booked in the opening minute, the defender brought down Bobzien as he threatened to break through on goal, receiving a second yellow card and leaving the visitors with ten men for the remainder of the contest.

Dresden looked increasingly comfortable against their numerical disadvantage, with Čović coming close to adding a fourth in the 73rd minute, only for his effort to be blocked by Krisztián Keresztes close to the goal line.

The hosts ultimately saw out a convincing 3-0 victory, recording another impressive home result following their recent wins over Magdeburg and in the cup against Schalke. The three points also provide a significant boost to Dresden's hopes of climbing away from the bottom of the 2. Bundesliga table, while Fürth will be disappointed with an evening in which defensive misfortune and Blank's dismissal contributed to a heavy defeat.

ATLANTA — The Nets have gone from suffering beatings to suffering heartbreakers.

From getting blown out to blowing late leads.

The Nets led almost all night here except when it mattered most, at the end. They committed a 124-121 collapse before a crowd of 16,117 at State Farm Arena on Saturday.

After looking in terrible disarray while dropping their first five games, the Nets (2-7) have split the past four. But those two defeats will stick in their collective craw.

Mikel Brown Jr. looks on during the Nets' 124-121 loss to the Hawks on Nov. 7, 2026 in Atlanta. NBAE via Getty Images

They blew a fourth-quarter lead in the Garden to the reigning champion Knicks. And Saturday, they squandered a 17-point cushion and had a 114-110 edge with 1:45 to play before allowing 10 unanswered points that cost them the game.

"We were not consistent enough to do the right things. And it's not about making shots, it's about trying to do the right things. Obviously, the points off turnovers, this is a team that will pressure you, and we had 22 turnovers for 28 points. That's not acceptable. That's where you lose the game," Nets coach Jordi Fernández said.

"Our effort was not great. We didn't do a lot of things. We didn't pay attention to details. Offensively, a lot of random stuff. So I guess we were just not really focused anymore," Nolan Traore said.

"We had great looks in the first half, but in the second half, we played more random stuff, so we didn't have the same quality shots. So that might be the main thing. I don't think Atlanta did something that disturbed us, it was more just us doing random stuff."

Julius Randle drives on Aaron Wiggins during the Nets' road loss to the Hawks. Getty Images

Brown scored 13 of his 18 points in the final period, but was a minus-10.

"Mikel had those five straight points, and I just let him roll because you cannot just keep taking them in and out," Fernández said when asked why he sat Traore. "When I was about to sub Nolan in, Mikel made two or three 3s and a midrange pullup. So I thought that was the right thing to do. Was it right? I don't know."

Fernández said the fact Brown was already slated to sit out Sunday's game in Dallas had nothing to do with the decision. He was just riding the hot hand.

Michael Porter Jr. drives to the basket during the Nets' road loss to the Hawks. Getty Images

Traore stormed out of the blocks with seven quick points to spot the Nets a 12-2 lead. And the bench helped pad it to 31-14 when Brown found Noah Clowney for a 3 with 3:57 left in the first quarter.

But shaky rebounding let the Hawks get on the offensive glass and cut that to 70-66 by the break.

It was still four at 114-110 after a Brown 3.

But that's when they allowed a 10-0 run to blow it.

Sharpe's turnover handed Onyeka Okongwu a 3, and after he missed a drive, Nickeil Alexander-Walker's free throw with 1:26 left put Atlanta up for good at 115-114.

When Porter missed a 3-pointer, Alexander-Walker raced for a loose ball and a breakaway layup. Both Sharpe and Julius Randle failed to corral rebounds and let the Hawks get second chances they cashed in on.

Johnson's and-one capped the 10-0 run with 38 seconds left and essentially ended it.

"They just started hitting shots down the stretch," Brown said. "Offensive rebounds, they were killing us all game. That was really the problem."

#2804. Mike Shanahan and Dan Reeves among Hall of Fame finalists

Dan Reeves and Mike Shanahan are one step closer to the Pro Football Hall of Fame. But that's likely where the journey will end, at least this year.

The Hall of Fame announced on Thursday that both former Denver Broncos head coaches were among the five former head coaches advanced by the Coach Subcommittee. Bill Belichick, Tom Coughlin, and Mike Holmgren were the other head coaches to advance. The next step in the process comes on Nov. 17, when the subcommittee will select one finalist to advance to the selection committee and present him for possible induction. After the presentation, the committee votes on whether to induct the former head coach.

Since only one head coach will be included in the 2027 enshrinement class, Belichick is the best bet. The fact that it's taken this long for Shanahan in particular to get inducted is absurd.

He's the winningest coach in Broncos history, and the Broncos are one of the most successful franchises in NFL history.

Shanahan is one of seven coaches to win back-to-back Super Bowls (Chuck Knoll did it twice with the Pittsburgh Steelers). Of those seven, four are in the Hall of Fame, with two as locks when the time comes for Bill Belichick (maybe?) and Andy Reid.

Including his time as a Broncos assistant, Shanahan is one of just six head coaches to earn at least 200 wins and multiple titles with a single franchise.

From 1996-98, Shanahan oversaw one of the most successful periods in NFL history. Denver won 46 games and two Super Bowls.

The Shanahan coaching tree and his offensive mind continue to influence the league in major ways.

His time as offensive coordinator with the San Francisco 49ers helped Steve Young win his first Super Bowl as a starting quarterback.

If that wasn't enough, here are some more tidbits to prove how incredible Shanahan was, especially in Denver.

The Broncos led the league in both 1,000-yard rushing seasons (11) and 1,000-yard receiving seasons (18) during Shanahan's 14 years as Denver's head coach.

As for Reeves, what he did with the Broncos is just as impressive as what former Buffalo Bills head coach and Hall of Famer Marv Levy did, yet Reeves' accomplishments are overlooked and underappreciated. Remember, Reeves was head coach for a team that went to three Super Bowls in four years.

Reeves won more than 60 percent of his games during his 12 seasons in Denver. But as the Broncos website points out, Reeves' candidacy extends beyond just the Mile High City. Reeves participated in nine Super Bowls as a player or coach, and he was a two-time AP Coach of the Year.

Shanahan should already be in the Hall of Fame, so hopefully it happens sooner rather than later. For Reeves, it'll take some time, but here's hoping he eventually gets his rightful place. Unfortunately, it'll be posthumously.

It's becoming clear that Broncos fans travel. We saw it a few weeks ago in Arizona against the Cardinals. But what I've seen the last few days in the Queen City is freaking impressive. Everywhere you look, there are Denver fans.

I won't predict what Bank of America Stadium will look like today, but there will be a lot of orange.

#2800. Knicks 109, Cavaliers 97: “ANOTHER GAME HOLDING THE BAD GUYS UNDER 100”

The Cavaliers (5-5) beat the Sixers at the Rocket Arena yesterday, so maybe you can blame their sulfurous, rotten-egg performance tonight on fatigue. In their first return to Ohio since sweeping the Eastern Conference Finals, the Knicks (5-4) picked up right where they left off. After piling on a 19-point lead in the third, our heroes let Donovan Mitchell (37 PTS, 13-22 FG) close the gap in the fourth, but he was outdueled yet again by Jalen Bruson (31 PTS, 12-25 FG), Karl-Anthony Towns (29 PTS, 13 RBS) was too strong, and the Knicks closed the door, 109-97.

Not only did our heroes knock off a rival, they played lock-down defense again. We share RJParrot's enthusiasm: "ANOTHER GAME HOLDING THE BAD GUYS UNDER 100."

Evan Mobley went right at Karl-Anthony Towns, who recorded his first foul with less than thirty seconds gone. Savvy strategy, Kenny Atkinson, but it wouldn't work tonight. After that foul, Towns did a good job of avoiding his second infraction for the rest of the half while still playing aggressively and collecting 18 points on 12 shots. He finished the game with two fouls. KAT's not just hungry for that second ring; I think he's gunning for MVP.

Josh Hart is still mending a sore ankle, so Landry Shamet started for him again. Shamet has proven to be an offensive weapon, but he attempted two shots in his 13 first-half minutes.

The Cavs had three rotation players on their injury report. With Jarrett Allen out, Meleek Thomas, the 34th pick in this year's draft, made his second start. The 20-year-old neophyte (9 PTS, 3-10 FG, 24 MIN) drilled back-to-back bombs to give his squad a 16-14 lead with five minutes left. Mike Brown used a timeout to regroup his squad and sub in Mohamed Diawara (2 PTS, 3 RBS, +16, 14 MIN) and Andre Drummond (8 RBS, 14 MIN). Soon after, Dalton Knecht (5 MIN) made his second appearance for the Knicks—and blundered by fouling Mitchell for what became a four-point play.

OAKAAKUYOAK Mario Hezonja is back in the league! He played nine minutes off the bench in the first half for the Ohio Players, scoring zero on two shots. Starter Peyton Watson (who was rumored to have a sore hammy) took six of Cleveland's first 13 shots, while Mobley had attempted none, Donovan Mitchell one, and James Harden two.

At the other end, Mike Brown was featuring Jalen Brunson and Towns. The latter made all four freebies at the line, while the former missed five of his first six shots. A slow start for Detective Madison, but stick around for sparks. Tyler Kolek also checked in to play alongside Knecht, Shamet, Anunoby, and Towns for the final two minutes. The Knicks were trailing by four, so the move was a vote of confidence by the coach.

With Towns and Anunoby smashing to the rim, the visitors were able to close the gap. The Knicks missed eight three-pointers in the opening frame, were outrebounded by three, and attempted half as many free throws as the Cavs, but nonetheless trailed by a single point at the break, 27-26. Math!

New York's awful long-range shooting persisted as they missed their first eight attempts of the second quarter. Mikal Bridges (9 PTS, 4-13 FG), in particular, had another woeful offensive half (during which he shot 0-5 from deep), but he redeemed himself with a few fine defensive efforts. Loved when he made the Beard look silly on a drive.

The ink still wet on his contract, Riley Minix provided eight points on 3-of-3 shooting off the bench tonight.

The scoreboard tilted back and forth. New York's shooting improved. Thomas checked back in for the hosts, and he drilled his third triple in Diawara's grill. The sophomore was +12 in the half, though, thanks to sharing the floor with Brunson, Jordan Clarkson, Bridges, and Drummond. Cap was cooking. He scored 18 straight Knicks points, outscoring the Cavs by seven himself and giving New York a 52–47 lead.

From there, McBride canned a jumper, Shamet drilled a dinger, and Anunoby hit consecutive triples to give the good guys a 63-53 advantage.

Through the half, both teams shot 44%, but the Knicks got 13 more shots, thanks to ten offensive boards. They also committed just three turnovers to the Cavs' eight and won the points-off-turnovers battle 12-2. The home team shot 46% from deep to New York's 32% and still trailed. Brunson topped the box score with 20 so far, while Spida led the Cavs with 11.

Cleveland opened the third with four straight points, both baskets set up by Donovan Mitchell, to cut the Knicks' lead to 63–57. Jalen Brunson then found Mikal Bridges for a three, bringing him to 9-34 from deep this season. Karl-Anthony Towns cut for a layup to stretch the lead back to 12.

Evan Mobley kept Cleveland close with six points in the opening five minutes, including back-to-back buckets off James Harden feeds. Tyrese Proctor's step-back three made it 72–65 after a Knicks possession that produced three misses, three offensive rebounds, and a shot-clock violation.

Brunson took over from there. He scored six straight on a floater, a running layup, and a fadeaway, then found Landry Shamet for a three to cap a 9–0 run. Mitchell broke it with a layup, but Brunson fed Mohamed Diawara for one of his own, sending Cleveland to timeout down 83–67. Very encouraging signs from Mo!

Towns chipped in four points, including a putback after Peyton Watson blocked his dunk attempt. OG Anunoby (15 PTS, 4-13 FG) had a block and two boards but missed all four of his shots and scored only at the line. Harden's two assists to Mobley helped briefly, but he went scoreless in the stretch. When Shamet swished his third triple of the night, New York's advantage was 19.

With the Knicks playing clean defense and the Cavs running on fumes, a 25-17 third quarter gave our heroes an 88-70 lead heading into the fourth.

The road got bumpy at the outset of the final frame. Kolek acquired his fourth foul; Shamet, Towns, and Anunoby missed multiple shots; and Mitchell and Mobley paired for eight points. Kolek's been a reliable floor general to head the second unit, but his shooting this season stands at 5-of-19 after tonight's 0-for-2. Seeing the need for heroics, Towns supplied them while Brunson sat. Smashing the boards and exploiting the false wall of Cleveland's frontcourt, he reached 29 points, logged his ninth double-double of the season, and scored five straight to restore a 15-point lead.

KAT sat at the middle mark. From there Cap and Spida traded blows. The latter scored Cleveland's next eight points, and with the score at 102-92, Mike Brown signaled for timeout with 3:15 remaining. Not ready to release his guys yet, Atkinson called for a timeout, too. Time for another Novig commercial.

Out of the break, Brunson and Mitchell traded contested jumpers. KAT was back, but Mobley boxed him out on a Brunson miss. Watson somehow corraled a slippery ball for a layup. Eight-point lead with 1:53 left.

The struggling Bridges came up with a clutch bucket. Shamet fouled Spida, who made one, missed one. Shamet missed from deep, but this time KAT got the board and pitched it to Cap, who was fouled. Just like Donovan, Jalen missed his first freebie. Mitchell tried a rushed trey with Shamet covering, which rimmed out. Anunoby grabbed the board; Spida swatted it out of bounds and got Kenny to contest it. Not only was the call confirmed, but a foul on the Cav was added to it. Insult to injury, you say? Indeed. Sweet victory!

Our heroes get two nights off before hosting the Bucks on Tuesday. Safe travels, Knickerbockers.

#2796. Sunday Patriots Notes: Christian Elliss continues to impress

It's a busy time in New England as the Patriots enshrined Rob Gronkowski in the team's Hall of Fame Saturday and will honor the 2016 Patriots team during halftime of Sunday's game against the Packers.

It has then been a busy week here on Pats Pulpit covering it all. So for anything that fell through the cracks, let's clean out the notebook from the week.

Welcome to the latest edition of our Sunday Patriots Notes.

As defensive coordinator Zak Kuhr takes the podium in front of the media every Thursday afternoon, the routine is usually typical.

Questions fly about the previous game or upcoming opponent. Schematic talk is usually brushed to the side. Questions about players usually revolve around blue chip talents like Christian Gonzalez or Milton Williams.

But Kuhr feels like one player in that group doesn't get enough attention.

"You didn't mention Christian Elliss," he said.

An undrafted free agent out of Idaho in 2021, Elliss began his career as a special teams player. That remained his role when he first joined the Patriots as a waiver claim late in the 2023 season, logging zero defensive snaps over the final four games.

Sticking in New England, Elliss went on to earn a consistent defensive role in 2024. His playing time has increased in each of the last three seasons, culminating in a full-time starting role this year. He has played 97% of the Patriots' defensive snaps in 2026 while starting 21 of their last 23 games.

"I think his consistency, and with him, I'd say even last year, starting off the first game, he'd admit to you, it was probably one of his worst games he's played," Kuhr said. "But his consistency has been his consistent improvement, and whether that be learning multiple roles now, being multiple packages, and yeah, I think he's just a great example to those younger guys."

The production has followed. The hard hitting Elliss has made an impact in every aspect on defense, recording 60 tackles, 1.5 sacks, four tackles for loss, six quarterback hits, a pass breakup and a forced fumble this season. His 11 pressures and 26 run stops are already career highs.

His play reached another level during the second half of last season, and that momentum has carried into 2026. Elliss credits a change in mindset for that development.

"I'm going to play free. I'm going to play with joy. That's the mentality I finally came to the conclusion of I need to have," he said last season. "I was slower in my play because I'm trying to make everything perfect. [Now], I've just kind of been like, screw that. I don't need it perfect. I'd rather have it be fast, physical, and, if I make a mistake, I'll do that going 100%."

After signing a two-year, $13.5 million contract extension with the Patriots in 2025, Elliss is set to become a free agent following the season. Given his role and his production this year, he has made a strong case to be a priority for another extension in New England.

Rob Gronkowski received his red jacket on Saturday as he was inducted into the Patriots Hall of Fame. Gronkowski and the 2016 Patriots will then be honored during Sunday's game to celebrate the 10-year anniversary of Super Bowl LI.

Drake Maye shared this week that he owned a Gronk jersey as a kid and was looking forward to reconnecting with the former tight end this weekend. The two have crossed paths a handful of times since Maye arrived in New England, with their first meeting coming at the 2024 Pro Bowl.

Maye has developed a strong connection with his own tight end during his Patriots career as Hunter Henry has climbed up the franchise ranks at the position. With Henry (foot) questionable for Sunday, it could mark Maye's first full game he's played as a Patriot without the veteran at his side.

"I think he's been someone for me that I can count on since my first snap in there my rookie year. He's been a security blanket and a great guy in the huddle," Maye said.

Sunday's game will be one for fans of the deep ball. Packers quarterback Jordan Love and Drake Maye are tied for the league lead in deep completions with 17 apiece. Love ranks first in deep passing yards (591), while Maye is second (586). Maye, meanwhile, leads the league in big-time throws targeting the deep area of the field (15), with Love ranking second (12).

Vrabel said the deep passing game starts with wide receivers who can get downfield and an offensive line that can hold up in protection. From there, it's up to the quarterback to deliver.

"Certainly, touch is involved, right? If you have to drive the ball, and arm strength," Vrabel said. "But I think probably just having a good feel of, 'Do I need a 35-yard pass that's in the air, or do I need a 50-yard ball?' and being able to judge that differently."

Patriots outside linebackers coach Mike Smith was on Green Bay's defensive staff when the Packers selected Jordan Love in the first-round of the 2020 NFL Draft. Smith noted how Love was a quiet rookie — a "pretty smart" move as he soaked up knowledge behind Aaron Rodgers.

Both Smith and Kuhr noted you see some resemblance of Rodgers in Love's game now as he has developed into one of the league's top quarterbacks.

"He's a really special player when he's at a full speed coming at you — at defenders. He's tough to guard, tough to handle. He's got great releases and just try to give him a chance to give him a ball to go catch," said Drake Maye about wide receiver Kyle Williams.

Patriots players and coaches have enjoyed having Terrell Williams back in the building and on the sideline during game days this season.

Kuhr called Williams a positive influence on his psyche as he instills confidence in the coordinator, while the assistant head coach's impact has reached all levels of the team.

"He touches all the players on both sides of the ball to get a feel for them and help them grow," Kuhr said. "And especially with these rookies, what they have to go through, he's just a great sounding board, great resource, advice, helps with the game-planning, but also does a good job of saying, like, 'This is your show.' "

The Patriots are one of the top special teams units in football when it comes to limiting touchbacks. On the year, just 7.7% of their kickoffs result in touchbacks while they're 0.4 touchbacks per game ranks fourth best in the league.

Head coach Mike Vrabel credited kicker Andy Borregales for his work in that aspect, while coordinator Jeremy Springer highlighted the need to cover kicks with the new rules.

"You got to be able to cover kicks in the NFL. That's the way it is now," Springer said. "I don't want them to start to drive at the 35 yard line. Every time you hit touchbacks, it's the 35 yard line.

"So, if we can get them inside the 30, inside the 25, or get a penalty, now they're on the 15, the 10, those are the hidden yards throughout the game that are going to help you win football games. The last thing you want to do is kick touchbacks."

The Patriots will change up the schedule this week with Sunday's game against the Detroit Lions in Munich, Germany.

This means Mike Vrabel media availability on Monday and an off-day on Tuesday will be regularly scheduled, before the team holds a normal Wednesday before departing to Germany that night. That's where they will practice on Thursday and Friday before kickoff on Sunday at 9:30 a.m. ET.

#2792. Nick Sirianni admits that he misled reporters about quarterback situation

How do you know when a football coach is lying? If he’s good at it, you don’t.

Because they all do. Particularly in so-called “must-lie” situations.

There’s an art to it. A way to conceal a lie with another lie. On Friday, Eagles coach Nick Sirianni opted not to lie about the fact that he lied on Monday when he told reporters that quarterback Tanner McKee would not be benched.

“Tanner’s our guy,” Sirianni said. “We’re not making any changes there.”

On Wednesday, the Eagles made a change there, elevating Joe Milton over McKee. The move was announced after Sirianni had his midweek media availability, which prevented him from being asked questions about the change in position from “Tanner’s our guy” to “Tanner’s not our guy.”

On Friday, Sirianni finally faced the music regarding his comments from Monday. In lieu of coming up with an explanation premised on the idea that what he said was true when he said it and circumstances changed, Sirianni surprisingly admitted that he wasn’t telling the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth to reporters and, in turn, the fans.

“I was going to hold onto that as long as I possibly could, every second, every minute,” Sirianni said. “Again, I’m not real shy with you guys. I’m going to tell you what I want to tell you guys. I respect the job that y’all have to do, but I’m going to tell you what I want to tell you guys because I’m always going to protect the team first and foremost.

“Every second that goes by in a situation like that, that you can hold onto information as long as you possibly can, is a little less time for the opponent to get ready for the game. I know there’s a lot of interest in everything that you all want to hear, the fans want to hear. My job is to win football games, do everything we can do to help win football games, protect the guys here on this football team, and handle everything that I can inside.”

In an industry where the truth is only told when it’s coincidental to strategic interests, it’s jarring that Sirianni told the truth that he was lying. It would have been easy to say, “We took a more careful look at the situation after Monday.” Or, even more simply, “We changed our mind. Shit happens.”

Instead, Sirianni opted to say, essentially, “Bullshit happens.” Instead of bothering to concoct a cover story regarding his lie, he said, essentially, “Yeah. I lied. I’ll do it whenever I feel like I have to.”

That’s the most important thing to remember. Coaches lie whenever they feel like they have to. Despite that fact, reporters and fans routinely take their words at face value, swallowing the bullshit while saying, “Thank you, sir, may I have another?”

So thank you, Nick, for making my job a little easier. In my first week of law school, one of the professors said, “The most important thing I can do for you is to give you a good crap filter.”

Because crap is everywhere. Usually, the people spewing it don’t admit it. When they do, it provides a tangible reminder as to whatever they say in the future.

For Sirianni, that’s the most problematic aspect of his decision to tell the truth about lying. There’s now an “Exhibit A” to which anyone and everyone can point as to anything and everything he says when assessing whether he’s being straight with reporters and, in turn, with fans.

#2789. Hawks' Jalen Johnson scores 30 in comeback from injury

Jalen Johnson scored 30 points in his return from an ankle injury and the Atlanta Hawks beat the Brooklyn Nets 124-121 on Saturday, Nov. 7 at State Farm Arena. The Hawks were down by as many as 17 points in the first quarter.

Johnson, 24, had 12 points points in the fourth quarter to bring his team back on top for good. With 39 seconds left in the game, he raced past Julius Randle and drove to the basket to toss in a floater. He was fouled and made the free throw to help secure the victory. The forward also had seven rebounds and six assists.

Nickeil Alexander-Walker and Aaron Wiggins added 20 points for Atlanta in the Hawks' fourth straight win. Michael Porter Jr. had 25 points for Brooklyn.

Johnson hadn't played in a week, missing three games after spraining his left ankle in the Hawks' loss to the New Orleans Pelicans on Halloween.

The day of the Nets matchup, he was listed as probable on the injury report and then was upgraded to available shortly before tipoff.

The Hawks took Johnson as the 20th overall pick in the 2021 NBA Draft. He earned his first All-Star nod last season when he 22.5 points, 10.3 rebounds and 7.9 assists per game.

He is averaging 18.3 points, 9.0 boards and 7.9 assists this season.

#2786. As Chargers look for answers, who is to blame for 0-7 start?

The Los Angeles Chargers' season has proven to be a complete failure.

The Chargers were predicted to be an above .500 team this season, but with a 0-7 start, the team now has very little wiggle room to even make that expectation a reality.

Coming off a bye week, the team did not appear to have taken any significant strides, suffering a 24-9 loss to the Los Angeles Rams at SoFi Stadium on Nov. 1.

The Chargers put together a promising first half, scoring nine points on three field goals.

One of the biggest positives from the half came in the final seconds of the second quarter when quarterback Justin Herbert threw a hail mary 54 yards to Ladd McConkey.

Unfortunately for the Chargers, McConkey was tackled at the one-yard line as time expired and went into the locker room without additional points.

The play didn't help create any momentum for the Chargers, who finished scoreless in the second half.

The Chargers will have the opportunity to turn things around against the Houston Texans on Sunday, Nov. 7, at home.

After seven consecutive losses this season, who is to blame for the disappointing start to the season?

There is a lot of blame that could be passed around regarding the team's recent on-field struggles.

Coach Jim Harbaugh, offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel and quarterback Justin Herbert are among the three in that order that should take on the bulk of that responsibility.

The Chargers moved away from being a pass-heavy offense that proved to be functional and efficient compared to what the offense has presented under McDaniel's watch this season.

Harbaugh added McDaniel to lead the offensive staff with the expectation that he would be an upgrade over what was already in place.

Herbert has been an above-average quarterback during his time in Los Angeles and he should be in the midst of a career year as a veteran and not regress with an uptick in interceptions.

As the head coach, Jim Harbaugh should take the brunt of the blame and responsibility.

He had the opportunity during the bye week to make much-needed changes to the offense but did nothing.

"We're aware of what the issues are, and we're the only ones that can fix them," Harbaugh told reporters on Nov. 1.

Harbaugh continued to get peppered with questions during the media availability but remained fairly vague.

"Our motivation is a dedication to getting it changed, getting it fixed," Harbaugh said when asked about keeping McDaniel.

While there was a pledge that some changes would be made, McDaniel remained as the playcaller through the bye week.

The Chargers have actually doubled down on their support and loyalty for one another.

Offensive lineman Joe Alt said the group remains bought in but admitted his displeasure with the results.

"Just frustrated," Alt said. "You want to come away with a win as a player and as a unit we have to be better. The scoreboard reflects that. … We have to score more points."

The offense has not scored a touchdown in its last nine quarters of play. It's a drought that spans 27 possessions.

Sean McVay vs Jim Harbaugh: Will Rams or Chargers figure things out?

As offensive coordinator with a clear directive from the head coach to score points, McDaniel's offense failed another test.

"We're not scoring enough points," Harbaugh said on Oct. 18 after a loss to the Kansas City Chiefs on the road.

McDaniel talked about collaborating with Herbert to help turn things around during the bye week. The coordinator called the bye week not much of a break, because "there were problems to solve."

The duo spent four hours watching film together throughout the week to "find spots to build on, where you can find spots to improve," but those again didn't necessarily result in touchdowns and a victory.

"In this league you have to produce results, or there's going to be heat, so I don't expect anything else," McDaniel said during a press conference on Oct. 29.

The heat is on, but it remains unclear when Harbaugh may be ready to make a change or if the organization will make it for him.

Last season, the Chargers had a middling offense under coordinator Greg Roman. It ranked 20th in the league with 21.6 points per game. The offense threw 14 interceptions and scored 36 total touchdowns.

This season, the Chargers rank last in scoring offense, averaging 14.1 points per game. The team is also averaging 310.9 total yards per game and has just nine total touchdowns through the first seven games.

Despite all the struggles Herbert has dealt with this season, he remains publicly bought into McDaniel's offense.

"I believe in him," Herbert said. "He's a great coach. He's very smart and it's on us as an offense to make those plays. ... We just have to make plays and score points and score touchdowns and we haven't done that for him."

Herbert completed 24 of 32 passes for 257 yards and two interceptions against the Rams on Sunday. He was also sacked twice.

"Whatever we've been doing hasn't been enough and it's up to us," Herbert said during the postgame press conference on Nov. 1. "Only we in the locker room can change it and work toward it."

Herbert has averaged 24 passing touchdowns and 9.7 interceptions per season through his career. This season has seen remarkable regression.

The star QB has completed 131 of his 212 pass attempts for 1,398 yards with just five touchdowns through the first seven games. He's already thrown 10 interceptions and has been sacked 23 times this season.

He's also second in rushing for the Chargers with 33 carries for 183 yards and three touchdowns.

"We don't really pay attention to the opinions of outside people," McDaniel told the media on Nov. 5. "People are saying whatever they want with whatever facts they have when we're not living up to expectations. ... Keep it moving."

#2785. Myles Garrett: Rams' opponents will have to pick their poison, me or Aaron Donald

Rams defensive end Myles Garret and defensive tackle Aaron Donald will finally be on the field together Sunday in Washington, and Garrett says that’s going to be bad news for opposing offenses for the rest of the season.

Donald did not play in Week 1 because he was still ramping up for the season after returning from his two-year retirement, and Garret hasn’t played since Week 1 because of knee surgery. Garrett said the two of them together, two multiple-time Defensive Player of the Year award winners side by side, will present a unique challenge for opposing offenses.

“I think offenses really have to pick their poison. Who’s going to be freed up this play? I think either of us are pretty good at winning one-on-one, so we’ll have some fun,” Garrett said. “Going into this season I never thought I’d have the chance, and as you all know he kept us in suspense for quite a while, so it was very exciting, and I’m looking forward to getting on the field and playing some real snaps with him.”

Garrett said his poor performance in Week 1 against the 49ers showed him he needed knee surgery, something he would have preferred to avoid.

“I was frustrated after the game. I knew that wasn’t me, and I was being hampered by something,” Garrett said. “I didn’t want to miss any time, but I had to be realistic about where I was physically, and I had to make the best choice for me and the team.”

But now Garrett is back, and he said he and Donald playing together can give the Rams an “elite defense” for the rest of the season.

#2784. Who is Joe Milton III? Eagles turn to QB with 'cannon' arm strength

Jordan Mailata might have been speaking for the rest of his Philadelphia Eagles teammates – and the public at large – when discussing his initial impression of quarterback Joe Milton.

"Have you seen his arm?" Mailata asked reporters on Wednesday, Nov. 4. "It is a (expletive) cannon, oh my God."

After taking a moment to apologize for his language, the left tackle went on to describe what made the passer such a singular player at the position.

"You see (the arm strength) on TV. You hear about it when he was going through the draft. But then you see it, and it's a work of art, man," Mailata said.

Since he was a high school football standout, Milton has been known for physical capabilities that differentiate him from even his most gifted peers. But after spending the bulk of his three-year pro career on the fringes of the league, the 6-5, 230-pound quarterback will get his chance to step into the spotlight Sunday, when he's set for his first pro start against the New York Giants.

Milton takes over for Tanner McKee, who started the past three games after Jalen Hurts was sidelined by blood clots that later moved to his lungs. Under McKee, an already shorthanded and struggling Eagles offense continued to flounder. The attack ranks last in yards per game (265.3) and 30th in scoring (17.1 points per game).

With the team's losing streak extending to six games, Milton is being called on to provide some kind of spark.

"With everything going on, he provides a good light to it," Mailata said of Milton.

From the time Milton started emerging as a highly sought-after high school recruit in Orlando, word began spreading about his arm strength.

As a 16-year-old, he threw a pass 75 yards to win a high-school competition, he said in 2024. At the Manning Passing Academy in 2023, Milton launched a pass more than 70 yards, with a clip of the feat quickly going viral.

For as easy as he made his throws look, though, college was anything but that for the quarterback. He lost his starting job twice – first at Michigan, then again at Tennessee after an injury.

But Milton put himself back into the NFL conversation with his final season with the Volunteers, during which he threw for 2,769 yards and 20 touchdowns with five interceptions. After again showcasing his unique physical tools during the pre-draft process, he was selected in the sixth round of the 2024 NFL Draft by the New England Patriots, who took fellow quarterback Drake Maye with the No. 4 overall pick.

Stashed as a developmental option, Maye didn't see any action until Week 18 of his rookie year, when he took over for Maye after one series and threw for 241 yards in a win over the Buffalo Bills. He delivered a signature moment when he repeatedly evaded rushers as he darted left before uncorking a 48-yard touchdown strike to Kayshon Boutte.

That performance caught the attention of Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones, who three months later acquired Milton in a trade with the Patriots.

"I really have to pinch myself that we got him after the last game that he had up there, starting there for New England," Jones told 105.3 The Fan in Dallas in August 2025. "I'm just excited that we had a chance to get him. And he hasn't disappointed. ... We're just more and more encouraged by what we're seeing."

But Milton lost the role as Dak Prescott's backup to Sam Howell prior to this season and was waived in late August as part of the team's cutdowns to a 53-man roster. He rejoined the Cowboys two days later, however, when he re-signed to the practice squad.

When the Eagles signed Milton to their practice squad on Oct. 16, one day before Hurts was placed on injured reserve, the move might have largely been an afterthought to some.

Less than a month later, however, he's taking on a starring role for the team at a crucial juncture.

Eagles coach Nick Sirianni initially said on Monday, Nov. 2, that he was not entertaining benching McKee. Two days later, news broke of the switch.

Sirianni later chalked up the mislead to a matter of trying to establish a competitive advantage.

"Every second that goes by in a situation like that, that you can hold onto that information as long as you possibly can, is a little less time for the opponent to get ready for the game," Sirianni said Friday, Nov. 6.

With the news out, however, Sirianni went to bat for his new starter.

"He's talented and been here for a couple weeks now," Sirianni said of Milton. "Very talented arm, very talented athlete, can process and make decisions out there. Lot of good qualities he has. I like his confidence and everything that he brings, and it's been fun getting to know him and working with him."

This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: Who is Joe Milton III? Eagles turn to QB with 'cannon' arm strength

#2782. Rams listed Matthew Stafford with elbow injury because reporters asked about ice on it

On Monday, reporters asked Rams coach Sean McVay about quarterback Matthew Stafford having ice on his throwing arm after Sunday’s win over the Chargers. On Wednesday, the Rams listed Stafford as having an elbow injury.

“Really, it’s because you guys asked me about it earlier in the week,” McVay told reporters on Friday regarding the decision to disclose an elbow injury for Stafford. “It’s more semantical than anything else. It’s normal, like what he told you guys, but because you guys asked me about him having ice on his elbow. . . . He’s been full, hasn’t missed any sort of reps so normal management stuff that he’s been doing over the last few years.”

It conjures memories of the Patriots’ one-time habit of listing former quarterback Tom Brady as “probable” with a “right shoulder” injury. That all started because he had ice on his shoulder in the locker room, reporters inquired, and the team decided to just put him on the injury report every week.

Has the elbow situation affected Stafford’s throwing?

“I haven’t seen any of that,” McVay said. “I told you guys he’d be better equipped to talk about it. He’s been a full participant, been awesome. He’s spinning the ball. He’s been able to activate all parts of the field with great timing, rhythm, and accuracy so he’s been great.”

So either he has an actual elbow injury that the Rams had been concealing, or he doesn’t really have an elbow injury but they listed him as having one because reporters noticed ice on his arm and asked McVay about it. Neither explanation seems to reflect the true spirit of the injury report, which expects real injuries — and only real injuries — to be disclosed.

Either Stafford has an elbow injury that was previously hidden or he doesn’t have an elbow injury and the claim that he has one is a middle finger to the meddling reporters who were doing their jobs. Neither explanation is a preferred alternative to the unvarnished truth.

The Cowboys placed outside linebacker Malachi Lawrence on injured reserve, the team announced Saturday.

Lawrence injured his ankle in Sunday’s loss to the Cardinals, and coach Brian Schottenheimer had announced the rookie would miss multiple weeks.

Lawrence will miss at least four games on IR.

The first-round pick has 13 tackles, a sack and three quarterback hits, while playing 41 percent of the defensive snaps.

In a corresponding move, the Cowboys activated outside linebacker Marist Liufau from injured reserve. Liufau broke his forearm in the preseason finale. He returned to practice Oct. 22.

Cowboys defensive tackle Jonathan Bullard, who is in his 21-day return-to-practice window, will remain on injured reserve. He has a calf injury but had full practices all week.

The Cowboys also announced they elevated wide receiver Jordan Hudson and tight end James Mitchell from the practice squad.

Tight ends Jake Ferguson and Luke Schoonmaker are questionable to play, and at wide receiver, KaVontae Turpin is out and George Pickens is questionable.
